10. Multilevel models

NoteAbout this chapter

The preregistered test of the training effects, outcome by outcome: one multilevel model per outcome with the interaction of wave and condition, questionnaires nested in persons nested in municipalities, and the same model with the trainers as a further level. Two further models replicate the effect when the control group trains, random slopes ask whether the change differs between trainers, municipalities and persons, also within each condition, and equivalence tests check the claims that the groups do not differ at baseline and after both trainings. Each of the 23 scales and the three hypothesis composites goes through the same eight steps. One-sided tests and a correction for testing many outcomes then show how much the counts of significant effects depend on these choices, and a table at the end puts all outcomes side by side. Feeds the preregistered results of Hypotheses 1 to 3.

source("R/packages.R")                  # all packages (Chapter 1)
source("R/settings.R")                  # waves, conditions, folders (Chapter 1)
df      <- readRDS("cache/df.rds")      # one row per questionnaire (Chapter 2)
df_wide <- readRDS("cache/df_wide.rds") # one row per person (Chapter 2)
item_names <- names(select(df, ListenOther1:CompetenceNonFrustrated4))
source("R/scales.R")                    # the 23 scales (Chapter 2)

10.1 How each outcome is examined

What happens to each outcome? The outcomes are the 23 scale scores and the three hypothesis composites (Chapter 2). Each goes through the same eight steps, in the same order and in four parts: the model, the effects, their robustness, and what follows. The diagram shows the path; the list below describes each step.

The eight steps in detail:

The model:

  1. The model. The preregistered multilevel model, outcome ~ Occasion * condition + (1 | Municipality/id): wave (T0 to T3) and condition as fixed effects with their interaction, and random intercepts for persons nested in municipalities, fitted by REML. The fixed effects are tested with Satterthwaite degrees of freedom (lmerTest). The intercept is the control group in January, conditionExperimental the difference of the experimental group in January, OccasionT1 to OccasionT3 the change of the control group since January. The model then goes through the textbook checks of a multilevel model (Zuur et al., 2009, ch. 5; Harrison et al., 2018): the estimation converged, and two other optimizers (bobyqa and Nelder-Mead) give the same fixed effects, the check lme4 recommends when it warns; no variance is estimated at zero (a singular fit); the residuals and the random intercepts of the persons are close enough to normal (skewness within ±2, excess kurtosis below 7; West, Finch & Curran, 1995); and the residuals spread about evenly over the eight cells of condition and wave, shown with a figure of the residuals against the normal distribution and against the fitted values.
  2. The random structure. Whether the municipality is a level of its own: the null model with persons nested in municipalities against persons alone, compared by AIC (lower is better), and how the variance is shared between municipalities, persons and the questionnaires of a person. The municipality level stays whatever AIC says: the conditions were assigned by municipality, so the design calls for it. Then the trainers, whom the preregistration names, together with their municipalities, as the random factor. Each trainer trained one municipality in each condition, so the municipalities are nested in the trainers. The model of step 1 with this further level is fitted with the bobyqa optimizer (with the default one, three of the 26 models stop short of convergence) and compared with the model of step 1 by AIC.

The effects:

  1. The interactions. Each interaction term OccasionTk:conditionExperimental compares the change from T0 to wave k between the groups (positive: the experimental group changes more), tested two-sided at α = .05, with and without the trainer level. The expectation: positive at T1 and T2, once the experimental group has trained and the control group not yet, and near zero at T3, after both have trained. A figure shows the means the model implies for both groups at each wave.
  2. One-sided tests. The hypotheses are directional. A one-sided test looks only in the expected direction: it halves the p of an effect that points there and gives an effect against the expectation a p above .5. Everywhere else the verdicts rest on two-sided tests; step 5 shows the one-sided p beside them. The correction for testing many outcomes at once needs the tests of all outcomes and follows in 10.7.
  3. The replication. Whether the control group gains when it trains, in two models. The period-specific model uses only the September and December waves, with condition × T3 (negative when the control group gains more); singular fits, where a variance is estimated at zero, are marked. The piecewise model uses all four waves, with one time indicator for each training (Chapter 2): conditionExperimental:Time_Exp_Training is the effect while the experimental group trains (T0 to T1, expected positive), conditionExperimental:Time_Control_Training the effect while the control group trains (T2 to T3, expected negative). For the composites a third model has a single indicator of being trained.

Robustness:

  1. Random slopes. Time is coded by Helmert contrasts (T0 against later waves; T3 against earlier waves, Chapter 2). Within one condition every municipality had the same schedule, so slope variance there is free of the training effect. In each condition separately, four likelihood-ratio tests on maximum-likelihood fits:
    • random slopes of both contrasts across municipalities, against random intercepts. Within one condition each trainer worked in exactly one municipality, so trainers and municipalities are the same ten groups and one level stands for both;
    • a random slope across persons, for each contrast on its own: both at once would need more random effects than there are questionnaires;
    • a fixed interaction of municipality and pre/post in the arm’s own training window (T0 to T1 in the experimental group, T2 to T3 in the control group): do the ten municipalities gain differently from their training?
    Slope variances near zero make single optimizers stop at different points, so every model is fitted with three and the best fit is kept. For the composites, random slopes of both contrasts at the trainer and municipality levels are also tested across both conditions.
  2. Equivalence. Two claims of the preregistration are claims of absence: the groups do not differ at baseline (condition at T0), and they no longer differ after both have trained (condition × T3). A non-significant test does not show absence; two one-sided tests (TOST) do, against a smallest effect of interest of Δd = ±0.20. Each coefficient of the model of step 1 is divided by the standard deviation of the outcome at T0. Equivalence holds when the 90 % confidence interval lies within ±0.20. The verdict sets the TOST beside the two-sided test: equivalent (only the TOST is significant), different but trivially small (both are), different (only the two-sided test is) or inconclusive (neither is). The same tests follow with another rule for the random structure, the richest whose variances all lie above zero: persons in municipalities in trainers, else persons in municipalities, else persons alone (fitted with bobyqa).

What follows:

  1. What follows. Where the result of the outcome goes next.

After the last outcome, 10.7 corrects the directional tests for the number of outcomes tested at once, and 10.8 sets all outcomes side by side.

10.2 Data and tools

Which data? All questionnaires (df, Chapter 2) for every model except the period-specific one of step 5, which takes the September and December waves alone:

# the 26 outcomes: the 23 scales and the three hypothesis composites
composites <- c("H1_ListeningTogetherness", "H2_CognitiveComplexity",
                "H3_Wellbeing")
outcomes   <- c(scales$scale, composites)

# the September and December waves, with an indicator of December
df_T23 <- df |>
  filter(Occasion %in% c("T2", "T3")) |>
  mutate(Time_T3 = if_else(Occasion == "T3", 1, 0))

# the smallest effect of interest of the equivalence tests (step 7)
sesoi <- .20

The slopes within the conditions (step 6) are 208 likelihood-ratio tests: 26 outcomes, two conditions, four tests, every model fitted with three optimizers. They take more than a minute and run as a script; each outcome section reads its eight tests from the result:

# Random slopes within each condition (Chapter 10.5): for the 23 scales and
# the three composites, in each condition separately, whether the change
# varies between municipalities and between persons, and whether the
# municipalities change differently in their own training window.
# Likelihood-ratio tests on maximum-likelihood fits (about 1.5 minutes).
# Run from swt-website/ after Chapter 2:  Rscript scripts/slopes_within.R

source("R/packages.R")
source("R/settings.R")
df <- readRDS("cache/df.rds")      # one row per questionnaire (Chapter 2)
item_names <- names(select(df, ListenOther1:CompetenceNonFrustrated4))
source("R/scales.R")               # the 23 scales (Chapter 2)

outcomes <- c(scales$scale, "H1_ListeningTogetherness",
              "H2_CognitiveComplexity", "H3_Wellbeing")
time     <- "TF_helmert + TS_helmert"   # the two time contrasts (Chapter 2)

# each arm's own training window: T0 to T1 (experimental), T2 to T3 (control)
training_window <- list(Experimental = c("T0", "T1"),
                        Control      = c("T2", "T3"))

# a maximum-likelihood fit with three optimizers, keeping the best: with slope
# variances near zero, single optimizers stop at different points
ml_fit <- \(formula, data) {
  fits <- map(c("bobyqa", "Nelder_Mead", "nloptwrap"), \(optimizer)
    suppressWarnings(suppressMessages(
      lmer(as.formula(formula), data = data, REML = FALSE,
           control = lmerControl(optimizer = optimizer)))))
  fits[[which.max(map_dbl(fits, logLik))]]
}

# likelihood-ratio test of a model against the same model with more terms
lr_test <- \(data, outcome, base, extended) {
  m0 <- ml_fit(str_c(outcome, " ~ ", base), data)
  m1 <- ml_fit(str_c(outcome, " ~ ", extended), data)
  chisq <- max(2 * (as.numeric(logLik(m1)) - as.numeric(logLik(m0))), 0)
  df    <- attr(logLik(m1), "df") - attr(logLik(m0), "df")
  tibble(chisq = chisq, df = df, p = pchisq(chisq, df, lower.tail = FALSE))
}

# the four tests of one outcome in one condition
within_condition <- \(outcome, group) {
  data <- df |>
    filter(condition == group) |>
    drop_na(all_of(outcome))
  window <- training_window[[group]]
  in_window <- data |>
    filter(Occasion %in% window) |>
    mutate(post = as.integer(Occasion == window[2]))
  bind_rows(
    "slopes, municipalities" = lr_test(data, outcome,
      str_c(time, " + (1 | Municipality) + (1 | id)"),
      str_c(time, " + (", time, " | Municipality) + (1 | id)")),
    "slope T0 vs. later, persons" = lr_test(data, outcome,
      str_c(time, " + (1 | id)"),
      str_c(time, " + (1 + TF_helmert | id)")),
    "slope T3 vs. earlier, persons" = lr_test(data, outcome,
      str_c(time, " + (1 | id)"),
      str_c(time, " + (1 + TS_helmert | id)")),
    "municipality x pre/post" = lr_test(in_window, outcome,
      "Municipality + post + (1 | id)",
      "Municipality * post + (1 | id)"),
    .id = "test")
}

slopes_within <- expand_grid(outcome   = outcomes,
                             condition = c("Experimental", "Control")) |>
  mutate(tests = map2(outcome, condition, within_condition)) |>
  unnest(tests)

saveRDS(slopes_within, "cache/slopes_within.rds")
slopes_within <- readRDS("cache/slopes_within.rds")

Which tools? The analysis of each step is written out for every outcome. The checks of Step 1, the path at the head of each outcome, the figure, the verdict of the equivalence tests, the names in the text and the tables that bring the outcomes together use small functions, defined once here:

  • Model checks
  • Path
  • Model-implied means
  • Verdicts
  • Names
  • All outcomes
  • Tables at a glance
# ✓ or ✗
mark <- \(x) if_else(x, "✓", "✗")

# skewness and excess kurtosis of a set of values
skew_of     <- \(x) mean((x - mean(x))^3) / sd(x)^3
kurtosis_of <- \(x) mean((x - mean(x))^4) / sd(x)^4 - 3

# whether a fit converged without lme4's warning
converges <- \(fit) {
  !any(str_detect(fit@optinfo$conv$lme4$messages %||% "", "converge"))
}

# the same model with two other optimizers: do they converge, and how far
# do their fixed effects lie from those of the model? (the check lme4
# recommends when it warns; see its help page on convergence)
other_optimizers <- \(fit) {
  refits <- c("bobyqa", "Nelder_Mead") |>
    set_names() |>
    map(\(optimizer) lmer(formula(fit), data = fit@frame,
                          control = lmerControl(optimizer = optimizer)))
  tibble(converge = all(map_lgl(refits, converges)),
         distance = max(map_dbl(refits, \(refit)
           max(abs(lme4::fixef(refit) - lme4::fixef(fit))))))
}

# the textbook checks of a multilevel model (Zuur et al., 2009, ch. 5;
# Harrison et al., 2018): did the estimation converge, and do two other
# optimizers give the same fixed effects; is no variance estimated at zero
# (a singular fit); are the residuals and the person intercepts close
# enough to normal (skewness within ±2, excess kurtosis below 7; West,
# Finch & Curran, 1995); and how evenly do the residuals spread over the
# eight cells of condition and wave
lmm_checks <- \(fit) {
  residuals <- residuals(fit)
  persons   <- ranef(fit)[[str_subset(names(ranef(fit)), "^id")[1]]][[1]]
  others    <- other_optimizers(fit)
  smallest  <- as_tibble(VarCorr(fit)) |>
    filter(grp != "Residual") |>
    slice_min(sdcor, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
  spread    <- tibble(residual = residuals,
                      cell = interaction(model.frame(fit)$condition,
                                         model.frame(fit)$Occasion)) |>
    summarise(sd = sd(residual), .by = cell)
  tribble(
    ~check, ~value, ~criterion, ~holds,
    "1 estimation: converged",
    if (converges(fit)) "yes" else "warning", "yes", converges(fit),
    "2 estimation: the same with bobyqa and Nelder-Mead",
    str_c(if (others$converge) "converge, " else "warning, ",
          "fixed effects within ", format(signif(others$distance, 1),
                                          scientific = FALSE)),
    "within .001", others$converge & others$distance < .001,
    "3 variances: none at zero",
    str_c("smallest SD ", sprintf("%.3f", smallest$sdcor), " (",
          str_remove(smallest$grp, ":Municipality"), ")"),
    "not singular", !isSingular(fit),
    "4 residuals: skewness", apa(skew_of(residuals), 2), "within ±2",
    abs(skew_of(residuals)) <= 2,
    "5 residuals: excess kurtosis", apa(kurtosis_of(residuals), 2),
    "below 7", kurtosis_of(residuals) < 7,
    "6 person intercepts: skewness", apa(skew_of(persons), 2),
    "within ±2", abs(skew_of(persons)) <= 2,
    "7 residuals: largest / smallest SD of the eight cells",
    sprintf("%.2f", max(spread$sd) / min(spread$sd)), "reported", NA
  ) |>
    mutate(holds = if_else(is.na(holds), "–", mark(holds)))
}

# what the checks say, in two or three sentences
lmm_sentence <- \(checks) {
  fails <- \(k) checks$holds[str_starts(checks$check, as.character(k))] ==
    "✗"
  value <- \(k) checks$value[str_starts(checks$check, as.character(k))]
  ratio <- value(7)
  # the level of the smallest variance, in words
  level <- c(Municipality = "municipalities", id = "persons",
             trainedBy = "trainers")[str_match(value(3), "\\((.*)\\)")[, 2]]
  smallest_sd <- str_extract(value(3), "[0-9.]+")
  if (!any(checks$holds == "✗")) {
    return(str_c("The model converges, two other optimizers give the same ",
                 "fixed effects, every variance lies above zero, and the ",
                 "residuals and the person intercepts stay within the ",
                 "bounds of normality; the residuals spread about evenly ",
                 "over condition and wave (the largest SD of a cell is ",
                 ratio, " times the smallest)."))
  }
  c(if (fails(1) && !fails(2)) {
      str_c("lme4 warns that its default optimizer stopped short of ",
            "convergence. Bobyqa and Nelder-Mead fit the same model without ",
            "a warning and agree with it on every fixed effect, to ",
            str_extract(value(2), "within .*"), ": the warning comes from ",
            "the boundary, a variance close to zero (the SD between ",
            level, " is ", smallest_sd, "), not from estimates that are ",
            "off, and the model of step 1 stands.")
    },
    if (fails(1) && fails(2)) {
      str_c("The estimation stops short of convergence, and other ",
            "optimizers do not repair it (", value(2), ").")
    },
    if (fails(3)) {
      str_c("A variance is estimated at zero, between ", level, ": the model ",
            "reduces to a simpler random structure, which leaves the fixed ",
            "effects as they are; step 7 repeats the claims of absence ",
            "with the richest structure whose variances all lie above ",
            "zero.")
    },
    if (fails(4) || fails(5) || fails(6)) {
      shape <- c(if (fails(4)) str_c("the residuals are skewed (", value(4),
                                     ")"),
                 if (fails(5)) str_c("heavy-tailed (excess kurtosis ",
                                     value(5), ")"),
                 if (fails(6)) str_c("the person intercepts skewed (",
                                     value(6), ")")) |>
        str_flatten_comma(last = " and ")
      top <- str_starts(value(4), "-")
      str_c(str_replace(shape, "^t", "T"), ": the answers crowd at the ",
            if (top) "top" else "bottom", " of the scale. The fixed effects ",
            "and their tests are robust to such departures in samples of ",
            "this size (Schielzeth et al., 2020), but little room is left ",
            "for a change.")
    }) |>
    str_flatten(" ")
}

# the residuals of a model against the normal distribution, and against
# its fitted values
plot_residuals <- \(fit) {
  points <- tibble(residual = residuals(fit), fitted = fitted(fit))
  bind_rows(
    points |>
      arrange(residual) |>
      mutate(x = qnorm(ppoints(n())), y = residual,
             panel = "residuals against the normal"),
    points |> transmute(x = fitted, y = residual,
                        panel = "residuals against fitted values")) |>
    ggplot(aes(x, y)) +
    geom_point(size = .8, alpha = .35, colour = "#2a78d6") +
    geom_abline(data = tibble(panel = "residuals against the normal"),
                aes(intercept = 0, slope = sd(points$residual)),
                colour = "#e34948", linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_hline(data = tibble(panel = "residuals against fitted values"),
               aes(yintercept = 0), colour = "#e34948",
               linetype = "dashed") +
    facet_wrap(~ panel, scales = "free_x") +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "residual") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
}
# an estimate with its p, as "b = 0.52, p = .003"
b_text <- \(b, p) str_c("b = ", sprintf("%.2f", b), ", p = ", apa(p, 3))

# the path of an outcome through the eight steps: the models of the steps,
# fitted here once more with the same formulas
outcome_path <- \(outcome, next_text) {
  model_of <- \(right, data = df, ...) {
    lmer(as.formula(str_c(outcome, " ~ ", right)), data = data, ...)
  }
  model   <- model_of("Occasion * condition + (1 | Municipality/id)")
  trainer <- model_of("Occasion * condition + (1 | trainedBy/Municipality/id)",
                      control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa"))
  aic_municipality <- AIC(model_of("1 + (1 | id)")) -
    AIC(model_of("1 + (1 | Municipality/id)"))
  aic_trainer <- AIC(trainer) - AIC(model)
  terms <- tidy(model, effects = "fixed")
  interactions <- terms |> filter(str_detect(term, ":"))
  period <- model_of("condition * Time_T3 + (1 | Municipality/id)",
                     data = df_T23) |>
    tidy(effects = "fixed") |>
    filter(str_detect(term, ":"))
  piecewise <- model_of(str_c("condition * (Time_Exp_Training + ",
                              "Time_Control_Training) + ",
                              "(1 | Municipality/id)")) |>
    tidy(effects = "fixed") |>
    filter(str_detect(term, "Control_Training"), str_detect(term, ":"))
  slopes <- slopes_within |> filter(outcome == .env$outcome)
  sd_T0 <- sd(df[[outcome]][df$Occasion == "T0"], na.rm = TRUE)
  claims <- terms |>
    filter(term %in% c("conditionExperimental",
                       "OccasionT3:conditionExperimental")) |>
    mutate(d = estimate / sd_T0, se_d = std.error / sd_T0,
           p_tost = pmax(pt((d + sesoi) / se_d, df, lower.tail = FALSE),
                         pt((d - sesoi) / se_d, df)),
           verdict = verdict_of(p_tost, p.value))
  checks <- lmm_checks(model)
  failing <- str_extract(checks$check[checks$holds == "✗"], "^[0-9]+")
  problems <- c(`1` = "a convergence warning", `2` = "optimizers disagree",
                `3` = "a variance at zero", `4` = "skewed residuals",
                `5` = "heavy-tailed residuals",
                `6` = "skewed person intercepts")
  tribble(
    ~Step, ~Question, ~Result, ~Next,
    "1", "Does the model pass the textbook checks?",
    if (length(failing) == 0) {
      "yes, all six"
    } else if (identical(failing, "1")) {
      str_c("a convergence warning, a false alarm: two other optimizers ",
            "agree")
    } else {
      str_flatten_comma(problems[failing], last = " and ")
    }, "random structure",
    "2", "Municipalities a level of their own? Trainers?",
    str_c(if (aic_municipality > 0) "municipalities: yes" else
            "municipalities: not by AIC, kept by design",
          "; trainers: ", if (aic_trainer < 0) "AIC lower" else "no"),
    "interactions",
    "3", "Does the experimental group change more (T1, T2, T3)?",
    str_c(str_extract(interactions$term, "T[1-3]"), ": ",
          b_text(interactions$estimate, interactions$p.value)) |>
      str_flatten("; "),
    "one-sided tests",
    "5", "Does the control group gain more while it trains?",
    str_c("September to December: ", b_text(period$estimate, period$p.value),
          "; piecewise: ", b_text(piecewise$estimate, piecewise$p.value)),
    "random slopes",
    "6", "Does the change vary within a condition?",
    str_c(sum(slopes$p < .05), " of ", nrow(slopes), " tests significant"),
    "equivalence",
    "7", "Alike at baseline and after both trainings (TOST)?",
    str_c("baseline: ", claims$verdict[1], "; after both: ",
          claims$verdict[2]), "what follows",
    "8", "Where next?", next_text, "")
}
# the means the model implies for both conditions at each wave; shaded the
# two training windows (experimental: T0 to T1, control: T2 to T3)
plot_means <- \(fit) {
  cells <- expand_grid(Occasion  = factor(c("T0", "T1", "T2", "T3")),
                       condition = factor(c("Control", "Experimental")))
  cells |>
    mutate(mean = predict(fit, newdata = cells, re.form = NA),
           wave = as.integer(Occasion) - 1) |>
    ggplot(aes(wave, mean, colour = condition)) +
    annotate("rect", xmin = 0, xmax = 1, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
             fill = "#eb6834", alpha = .08) +
    annotate("rect", xmin = 2, xmax = 3, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
             fill = "#2a78d6", alpha = .08) +
    geom_line(linewidth = .8) +
    geom_point(size = 2.4) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(Control      = "#2a78d6",
                                   Experimental = "#eb6834")) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:3,
                       labels = str_c("T", 0:3, "\n", months_list)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "model-implied mean", colour = NULL,
         caption = str_c("shaded: the training of the experimental group ",
                         "(left) and of the control group (right)")) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), legend.position = "top")
}
# the verdict of an equivalence test, next to the two-sided test
verdict_of <- \(p_tost, p_two_sided) case_when(
  p_tost < .05 & p_two_sided >= .05 ~ "equivalent",
  p_tost < .05                      ~ "different but trivially small",
  p_two_sided < .05                 ~ "different",
  .default                          = "inconclusive"
)
# readable names of the outcomes, for the text
composite_labels <- c(H1_ListeningTogetherness = "Listening and Togetherness",
                      H2_CognitiveComplexity   = "Cognitive Complexity",
                      H3_Wellbeing             = "Well-being")
label_of <- \(outcome) {
  coalesce(scales$label[match(outcome, scales$scale)],
           unname(composite_labels[outcome]))
}
# the objects of each outcome section carry its prefix: lo_model, ...
prefixes <- c(ListenOther = "lo", ListenSelf = "lse", Understood = "und",
              KamaMuta = "km", Resonance = "res", Belongingness = "bel",
              NoAlienation = "nal", NoIsolation = "nis", Rogerian = "rog",
              ParadoxMindset = "pm", IntellectualHumility = "ih",
              ToleranceDiversity = "td", womenAttitude = "wa",
              Flourishing = "fl", AutonomySatisfaction = "asat",
              RelatednessSatisfaction = "rsat",
              CompetenceSatisfaction = "csat",
              AutonomyNonFrustrated = "anf",
              RelatednessNonFrustrated = "rnf",
              CompetenceNonFrustrated = "cnf", Empowerment = "emp",
              Agency = "ag", IntellectualCapital = "ic",
              H1_ListeningTogetherness = "h1",
              H2_CognitiveComplexity = "h2", H3_Wellbeing = "h3")

# one kind of object from all 26 sections, named by outcome:
# from_sections("model") gives lo_model, lse_model, ...
from_sections <- \(kind) {
  mget(str_c(prefixes[outcomes], "_", kind), inherits = TRUE) |>
    set_names(outcomes)
}
# an estimate with its p in brackets
b_and_p <- \(b, p) {
  str_c(sprintf("%.2f", b), " (", if_else(p < .001, "<.001", apa(p, 3)),
        ")")
}

# a Δd with its 90 % interval
d_and_ci <- \(d, low, high) sprintf("%.2f [%.2f, %.2f]", d, low, high)

10.3 Listening and togetherness (H1)

Others Listen to Me

Its path through the steps. One row per step below, from the models of the steps, fitted once more; every step uses both groups both groups:

Step Question Result Next
1 Does the model pass the textbook checks? yes, all six random structure
2 Municipalities a level of their own? Trainers? municipalities: yes; trainers: no interactions
3 Does the experimental group change more (T1, T2, T3)? T1: b = 0.82, p = .002; T2: b = 0.78, p = .006; T3: b = 0.03, p = .916 one-sided tests
5 Does the control group gain more while it trains? September to December: b = -0.87, p = .004; piecewise: b = -0.78, p = .007 random slopes
6 Does the change vary within a condition? 2 of 8 tests significant equivalence
7 Alike at baseline and after both trainings (TOST)? baseline: different; after both: inconclusive what follows
8 Where next? Chapter 20; 10.7

The model · Steps 1 and 2

Step 1 · The model both groups

Which model tests the training? The preregistered model: the score at each wave, with wave, condition and their interaction as fixed effects, and questionnaires nested in persons nested in municipalities:

lo_model <- lmer(ListenOther ~ Occasion * condition +
                   (1 | Municipality/id),
                 data = df)

lo_fixed <- tidy(lo_model, effects = "fixed") |>
  select(term, b = estimate, se = std.error, df, p = p.value)

lo_fixed |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))
term b se df p
(Intercept) 5.859 0.202 29.582 0.000
OccasionT1 0.351 0.186 744.212 0.060
OccasionT2 0.303 0.189 845.116 0.110
OccasionT3 1.502 0.196 827.871 0.000
conditionExperimental -0.585 0.286 30.366 0.050
OccasionT1:conditionExperimental 0.818 0.260 743.028 0.002
OccasionT2:conditionExperimental 0.779 0.284 820.517 0.006
OccasionT3:conditionExperimental 0.033 0.314 797.694 0.916

In January the control group averages 5.86 on the scale from 0 to 10; the experimental group starts 0.59 points lower, significantly so (p = .0497).

Does the model pass the textbook checks? Convergence, the same fixed effects with two other optimizers, no variance at zero, residuals and person intercepts close to normal, and the spread of the residuals over condition and wave:

lo_checks <- lmm_checks(lo_model)
lo_checks
check value criterion holds
1 estimation: converged yes yes ✓
2 estimation: the same with bobyqa and Nelder-Mead converge, fixed effects within 0.0000002 within .001 ✓
3 variances: none at zero smallest SD 0.396 (Municipality) not singular ✓
4 residuals: skewness -.35 within ±2 ✓
5 residuals: excess kurtosis .78 below 7 ✓
6 person intercepts: skewness -.14 within ±2 ✓
7 residuals: largest / smallest SD of the eight cells 1.38 reported – 
plot_residuals(lo_model)

The model converges, two other optimizers give the same fixed effects, every variance lies above zero, and the residuals and the person intercepts stay within the bounds of normality; the residuals spread about evenly over condition and wave (the largest SD of a cell is 1.38 times the smallest).

Next → Step 2, the random structure: Is the municipality a level of its own?

Step 2 · The random structure both groups

Is the municipality a level of its own? The null model with persons nested in municipalities, against persons alone:

lo_null_person <- lmer(ListenOther ~ 1 + (1 | id),
                       data = df)
lo_null_nested <- lmer(ListenOther ~ 1 + (1 | Municipality/id),
                       data = df)

AIC(lo_null_person, lo_null_nested) |>
  mutate(AIC = round(AIC, 1))
df AIC
lo_null_person 3 4930.5
lo_null_nested 4 4924.6

How is the variance shared? In the null model with both levels:

lo_shares <- as_tibble(VarCorr(lo_null_nested)) |>
  transmute(level = grp, variance = vcov, share = vcov / sum(vcov))

lo_shares |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))
level variance share
id:Municipality 1.890 0.369
Municipality 0.186 0.036
Residual 3.044 0.595

And the trainers? The model of step 1 with the trainers as a further level, and its variances:

lo_trainer <- lmer(ListenOther ~ Occasion * condition +
                     (1 | trainedBy/Municipality/id),
                   data = df,
                   control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa"))

AIC(lo_model, lo_trainer) |>
  mutate(AIC = round(AIC, 1))
df AIC
lo_model 11 4826.6
lo_trainer 12 4828.6 
lo_trainer_shares <- as_tibble(VarCorr(lo_trainer)) |>
  transmute(level = grp, variance = vcov, share = vcov / sum(vcov))

lo_trainer_shares |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))
level variance share
id:Municipality:trainedBy 2.050 0.426
Municipality:trainedBy 0.157 0.033
trainedBy 0.000 0.000
Residual 2.602 0.541

AIC prefers persons nested in municipalities to persons alone, by 5.9 points. Of the variance, 3.6 % lies between the municipalities, 36.9 % between the persons of a municipality and 59.5 % between the questionnaires of a person. The trainer level takes up none of the variance and only adds a parameter: the AIC rises by 2.0 points. The model of step 1 stays.

Next → Step 3, the interactions: Does the experimental group change more?

The effects · Steps 3 to 5

Step 3 · The interactions both groups

Does the experimental group change more? The three interaction terms, with and without the trainer level:

lo_trainer_fixed <- tidy(lo_trainer, effects = "fixed") |>
  select(term, b_trainer = estimate, p_trainer = p.value)

lo_interactions <- lo_fixed |>
  filter(str_detect(term, ":")) |>
  left_join(lo_trainer_fixed, by = "term")

lo_interactions |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))
term b se df p b_trainer p_trainer
OccasionT1:conditionExperimental 0.818 0.260 743.028 0.002 0.818 0.002
OccasionT2:conditionExperimental 0.779 0.284 820.517 0.006 0.779 0.006
OccasionT3:conditionExperimental 0.033 0.314 797.694 0.916 0.033 0.916

What does the model imply? The means of both groups at each wave; shaded the two training windows:

plot_means(lo_model)

By T1 the experimental group has gained more than the control group (b = 0.82, p = .002), and it keeps its advantage at T2 (b = 0.78, p = .006). At T3, after the control group’s training, the change since January no longer differs significantly (b = 0.03, p = .916). With the trainer level, the three terms stay the same to three decimals and keep their verdicts.

Next → Step 4, one-sided tests: Does it hold one-sided?

Step 4 · One-sided tests both groups

Does it hold one-sided? The effects at T1 and T2, where the hypotheses expect a positive sign:

lo_one_sided <- lo_interactions |>
  filter(term != "OccasionT3:conditionExperimental") |>
  transmute(term, b, p, p_one_sided = pt(b / se, df, lower.tail = FALSE))

lo_one_sided |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))
term b p p_one_sided
OccasionT1:conditionExperimental 0.818 0.002 0.001
OccasionT2:conditionExperimental 0.779 0.006 0.003

One-sided, both effects remain significant (p < .001 at T1, p = .003 at T2).

Next → Step 5, the replication: Does the control group gain when it trains?

Step 5 · The replication both groups

Does the control group gain when it trains? The period-specific model, on the September and December waves:

lo_period <- lmer(ListenOther ~ condition * Time_T3 +
                    (1 | Municipality/id),
                  data = df_T23)

lo_period_terms <- tidy(lo_period, effects = "fixed") |>
  filter(str_detect(term, ":")) |>
  transmute(term, b = estimate, se = std.error, df, p = p.value,
            singular = isSingular(lo_period))

lo_period_terms |>
  mutate(p_one_sided = pt(-b / se, df, lower.tail = FALSE),
         across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))
term b se df p singular p_one_sided
conditionExperimental:Time_T3 -0.866 0.296 235.052 0.004 FALSE 0.002

And over all four waves? The piecewise model, with one time indicator for each training:

lo_piecewise <- lmer(ListenOther ~ condition *
                       (Time_Exp_Training + Time_Control_Training) +
                       (1 | Municipality/id),
                     data = df)

lo_piecewise_terms <- tidy(lo_piecewise, effects = "fixed") |>
  filter(str_detect(term, ":")) |>
  transmute(term, b = estimate, se = std.error, df, p = p.value)

lo_piecewise_terms |>
  mutate(expected    = if_else(str_detect(term, "Time_Exp"), 1, -1),
         p_one_sided = pt(expected * b / se, df, lower.tail = FALSE),
         across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))
term b se df p expected p_one_sided
conditionExperimental:Time_Exp_Training 0.810 0.228 776.822 0.000 1 0.000
conditionExperimental:Time_Control_Training -0.777 0.288 762.401 0.007 -1 0.004

Between September and December, while the control group trains, it gains more than the experimental group (b = -0.87, p = .004). In the piecewise model the experimental group gains more while it trains (b = 0.81, p < .001), and the control group gains more while it trains (b = -0.78, p = .007).

Next → Step 6, random slopes: Does the change vary within each condition?

Robustness · Steps 6 and 7

Step 6 · Random slopes both groups

Does the change vary within each condition? The eight tests of the script (10.2), four in each condition:

lo_slopes_within <- slopes_within |>
  filter(outcome == "ListenOther") |>
  select(-outcome)

lo_slopes_within |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))
condition test chisq df p
Experimental slopes, municipalities 1.084 5 0.955
Experimental slope T0 vs. later, persons 1.119 2 0.571
Experimental slope T3 vs. earlier, persons 1.043 2 0.594
Experimental municipality x pre/post 12.694 9 0.177
Control slopes, municipalities 21.776 5 0.001
Control slope T0 vs. later, persons 14.269 2 0.001
Control slope T3 vs. earlier, persons 4.194 2 0.123
Control municipality x pre/post 12.989 9 0.163

Two of the eight tests are significant, both in the control group: the slopes across municipalities and the slope of T0 against later across persons. In neither condition do the municipalities gain differently from their own training.

Next → Step 7, equivalence: Which random structure is the richest?

Step 7 · Equivalence both groups

Which random structure is the richest? The model of step 1 under the three structures, fitted with bobyqa, and the smallest variance of each:

lo_structures <- list(
  `(1 | trainedBy/Municipality/id)` = lo_trainer,
  `(1 | Municipality/id)` =
    lmer(ListenOther ~ Occasion * condition +
           (1 | Municipality/id),
         data = df, control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")),
  `(1 | id)` =
    lmer(ListenOther ~ Occasion * condition +
           (1 | id),
         data = df, control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")))

lo_variances <- lo_structures |>
  map(\(fit) as_tibble(VarCorr(fit))) |>
  list_rbind(names_to = "structure") |>
  summarise(smallest = min(vcov), .by = structure) |>
  mutate(above_zero = smallest >= 1e-8)

lo_variances |>
  mutate(smallest = sprintf("%.1e", smallest))
structure smallest above_zero
(1 | trainedBy/Municipality/id) 2.4e-13 FALSE
(1 | Municipality/id) 1.6e-01 TRUE
(1 | id) 2.2e+00 TRUE 
# the first structure whose variances all lie above zero
lo_richest <- lo_variances$structure[lo_variances$above_zero][1]

Do the groups really not differ? The two claims of absence, at baseline and after both trainings, with the preregistered and with the richest structure:

lo_sd_T0 <- sd(df$ListenOther[df$Occasion == "T0"], na.rm = TRUE)

lo_tost <- bind_rows(
  preregistered = tidy(lo_model, effects = "fixed"),
  richest       = tidy(lo_structures[[lo_richest]], effects = "fixed"),
  .id = "model") |>
  filter(term %in% c("conditionExperimental",
                     "OccasionT3:conditionExperimental")) |>
  transmute(model,
            claim   = if_else(term == "conditionExperimental", "baseline",
                              "after_both"),
            term,
            delta_d = estimate / lo_sd_T0,
            se_d    = std.error / lo_sd_T0,
            ci_low  = delta_d - qt(.95, df) * se_d,
            ci_high = delta_d + qt(.95, df) * se_d,
            p_tost  = pmax(pt((delta_d + sesoi) / se_d, df,
                              lower.tail = FALSE),
                           pt((delta_d - sesoi) / se_d, df)),
            p_two_sided = p.value,
            verdict = verdict_of(p_tost, p_two_sided))

lo_tost |>
  select(model, claim, delta_d, ci_low, ci_high, p_tost, p_two_sided,
         verdict) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))
model claim delta_d ci_low ci_high p_tost p_two_sided verdict
preregistered baseline -0.255 -0.466 -0.043 0.668 0.050 different
preregistered after_both 0.014 -0.210 0.239 0.087 0.916 inconclusive
richest baseline -0.255 -0.466 -0.043 0.668 0.050 different
richest after_both 0.014 -0.210 0.239 0.087 0.916 inconclusive

Neither claim of absence can be shown. At baseline the groups differ: the experimental group starts lower (Δd = -0.25, 90 % CI [-0.47, -0.04]). After both trainings the test is inconclusive (Δd = 0.01, 90 % CI [-0.21, 0.24]). The richest structure with all variances above zero is persons in municipalities, as in the preregistered model; it gives the same verdicts, and Δd stays the same to three decimals.

Next → Step 8, what follows: Where does the result go?

What follows · Step 8

Step 8 · What follows

Where does the result go? Others Listen to Me shows the training effect in both windows: the experimental group gains more while it trains, keeps its advantage until September, and the control group catches up while it trains. Its interaction at T1 and its piecewise terms go to the comparison of the estimates in Chapter 20, its directional tests to the correction for many outcomes in 10.7.

                     (1 | Municipality/id),
                   data = df_T23)

lse_period_terms <- tidy(lse_period, effects = "fixed") |>
  filter(str_detect(term, ":")) |>
  transmute(term, b = estimate, se = std.error, df, p = p.value,
            singular = isSingular(lse_period))

lse_period_terms |>
  mutate(p_one_sided = pt(-b / se, df, lower.tail = FALSE),
         across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))
term b se df p singular p_one_sided
conditionExperimental:Time_T3 -1.188 0.273 253.966 0 FALSE 0

And over all four waves? The piecewise model, with one time indicator for each training:

lse_piecewise <- lmer(ListenSelf ~ condition *
                        (Time_Exp_Training + Time_Control_Training) +
                        (1 | Municipality/id),
                      data = df)

lse_piecewise_terms <- tidy(lse_piecewise, effects = "fixed") |>
  filter(str_detect(term, ":")) |>
  transmute(term, b = estimate, se = std.error, df, p = p.value)

lse_piecewise_terms |>
  mutate(expected    = if_else(str_detect(term, "Time_Exp"), 1, -1),

         across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))

Between September and December, while the control group trains, it gains more than the experimental group (b = -1.19, p < .001). In the piecewise model the experimental group gains more while it trains (b = 0.58, p = .002), and the control group gains more while it trains (b = -1.07, p < .001).

condition test chisq df p

Next → Step 7, equivalence: Which random structure is the richest?

Step 7 · Equivalence both groups

Which random structure is the richest? The model of step 1 under the three structures, fitted with bobyqa, and the smallest variance of each:

lse_structures <- list(
  `(1 | trainedBy/Municipality/id)` = lse_trainer,
  `(1 | Municipality/id)` =
    lmer(ListenSelf ~ Occasion * condition +
           (1 | Municipality/id),
         data = df, control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")),
  `(1 | id)` =
    lmer(ListenSelf ~ Occasion * condition +
           (1 | id),
         data = df, control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")))

lse_variances <- lse_structures |>
  map(\(fit) as_tibble(VarCorr(fit))) |>
  list_rbind(names_to = "structure") |>
  summarise(smallest = min(vcov), .by = structure) |>
  mutate(above_zero = smallest >= 1e-8)

lse_variances |>
  mutate(smallest = sprintf("%.1e", smallest))
structure smallest above_zero
(1 | trainedBy/Municipality/id) 0.0e+00 FALSE
(1 | Municipality/id) 1.1e-01 TRUE
(1 | id) 1.5e+00 TRUE 
# the first structure whose variances all lie above zero
lse_richest <- lse_variances$structure[lse_variances$above_zero][1]

Do the groups really not differ? The two claims of absence, at baseline and after both trainings, with the preregistered and with the richest structure:

lse_sd_T0 <- sd(df$ListenSelf[df$Occasion == "T0"], na.rm = TRUE)

lse_tost <- bind_rows(
  preregistered = tidy(lse_model, effects = "fixed"),
  richest       = tidy(lse_structures[[lse_richest]], effects = "fixed"),
  .id = "model") |>
  filter(term %in% c("conditionExperimental",
                     "OccasionT3:conditionExperimental")) |>
  transmute(model,
            claim   = if_else(term == "conditionExperimental", "baseline",
                              "after_both"),
            term,
            delta_d = estimate / lse_sd_T0,
            se_d    = std.error / lse_sd_T0,
            ci_low  = delta_d - qt(.95, df) * se_d,
            ci_high = delta_d + qt(.95, df) * se_d,
            p_tost  = pmax(pt((delta_d + sesoi) / se_d, df,
                              lower.tail = FALSE),
                           pt((delta_d - sesoi) / se_d, df)),
            p_two_sided = p.value,
            verdict = verdict_of(p_tost, p_two_sided))

lse_tost |>
  select(model, claim, delta_d, ci_low, ci_high, p_tost, p_two_sided,
         verdict) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))
model claim delta_d ci_low ci_high p_tost p_two_sided verdict
preregistered baseline -0.056 -0.257 0.145 0.117 0.641 inconclusive
preregistered after_both -0.246 -0.462 -0.031 0.637 0.060 inconclusive
richest baseline -0.056 -0.257 0.145 0.117 0.641 inconclusive
richest after_both -0.246 -0.462 -0.031 0.637 0.060 inconclusive

Neither claim of absence can be shown. Both tests are inconclusive, as their intervals reach beyond ±0.20: at baseline Δd = -0.06, 90 % CI [-0.26, 0.15], after both trainings Δd = -0.25, 90 % CI [-0.46, -0.03]. The richest structure with all variances above zero is persons in municipalities, as in the preregistered model; it gives the same verdicts, and Δd stays the same to three decimals.

Next → Step 8, what follows: Where does the result go?

What follows · Step 8

Step 8 · What follows

Where does the result go? I Listen shows the same pattern as Others Listen to Me: the effect in both training windows, and an advantage of the experimental group that lasts until the control group trains. Its interaction at T1 and its piecewise terms go to the comparison of the estimates in Chapter 20, its directional tests to the correction for many outcomes in 10.7.

What does the model imply? The means of both groups at each wave; shaded the two training windows:

plot_means(und_model)

By T1 the experimental group has not gained significantly more than the control group (b = 0.19, p = .387); at T2, however, it is ahead (b = 0.64, p = .007). At T3, after the control group’s training, the change since January no longer differs significantly (b = -0.19, p = .469). With the trainer level, the three terms stay the same to three decimals and keep their verdicts.

Does the experimental group change more? The three interaction terms, with and without the trainer level:

km_trainer_fixed <- tidy(km_trainer, effects = "fixed") |>
  select(term, b_trainer = estimate, p_trainer = p.value)

km_interactions <- km_fixed |>
  filter(str_detect(term, ":")) |>
  left_join(km_trainer_fixed, by = "term")

km_interactions |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))
term b se df p b_trainer p_trainer
OccasionT1:conditionExperimental 0.100 0.214 732.456 0.641 0.099 0.642
OccasionT2:conditionExperimental -0.154 0.234 809.963 0.509 -0.152 0.515
OccasionT3:conditionExperimental -0.649 0.259 786.972 0.012 -0.644 0.013

What does the model imply? The means of both groups at each wave; shaded the two training windows:

plot_means(km_model)

By T1 the experimental group has not gained significantly more than the control group (b = 0.10, p = .641), nor by T2 (b = -0.15, p = .509). At T3, after its own training, the control group has gained more since January (b = -0.65, p = .012). With the trainer level, the three terms move by at most 0.005 and keep their verdicts.

Next → Step 4, one-sided tests: Does it hold one-sided?

Step 4 · One-sided tests both groups

Does it hold one-sided? The effects at T1 and T2, where the hypotheses expect a positive sign:

km_one_sided <- km_interactions |>
  filter(term != "OccasionT3:conditionExperimental") |>
  transmute(term, b, p, p_one_sided = pt(b / se, df, lower.tail = FALSE))

km_one_sided |>

term b p p_one_sided
OccasionT1:conditionExperimental 0.100 0.641 0.320
OccasionT2:conditionExperimental -0.154 0.509 0.746

One-sided, the effect at T1 remains non-significant (p = .320), the one at T2 points against the expectation (p = .746).

Next → Step 5, the replication: Does the control group gain when it trains?

Step 5 · The replication both groups

Does the control group gain when it trains? The period-specific model, on the September and December waves:

km_period <- lmer(KamaMuta ~ condition * Time_T3 +
                    (1 | Municipality/id),
                  data = df_T23)

km_period_terms <- tidy(km_period, effects = "fixed") |>
  filter(str_detect(term, ":")) |>
  transmute(term, b = estimate, se = std.error, df, p = p.value,
            singular = isSingular(km_period))

km_period_terms |>
  mutate(p_one_sided = pt(-b / se, df, lower.tail = FALSE),
         across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))
term b se df p singular p_one_sided
conditionExperimental:Time_T3 -0.621 0.262 227.886 0.019 FALSE 0.009

And over all four waves? The piecewise model, with one time indicator for each training:

km_piecewise <- lmer(KamaMuta ~ condition *
                       (Time_Exp_Training + Time_Control_Training) +
                       (1 | Municipality/id),
                     data = df)

km_piecewise_terms <- tidy(km_piecewise, effects = "fixed") |>
  filter(str_detect(term, ":")) |>
  transmute(term, b = estimate, se = std.error, df, p = p.value)

km_piecewise_terms |>
  mutate(expected    = if_else(str_detect(term, "Time_Exp"), 1, -1),
         p_one_sided = pt(expected * b / se, df, lower.tail = FALSE),
         across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))
term b se df p expected p_one_sided
conditionExperimental:Time_Exp_Training -0.014 0.187 766.853 0.941 1 0.529
conditionExperimental:Time_Control_Training -0.619 0.238 752.774 0.010 -1 0.005

Between September and December, while the control group trains, it gains more than the experimental group (b = -0.62, p = .019). In the piecewise model the experimental group’s training window shows no significant effect (b = -0.01, p = .941), and the control group gains more while it trains (b = -0.62, p = .010).

km_slopes_within <- slopes_within |>

Next → Step 7, equivalence: Which random structure is the richest?

Step 7 · Equivalence both groups

Which random structure is the richest? The model of step 1 under the three structures, fitted with bobyqa, and the smallest variance of each:

km_structures <- list(
  `(1 | trainedBy/Municipality/id)` = km_trainer,
  `(1 | Municipality/id)` =
    lmer(KamaMuta ~ Occasion * condition +
           (1 | Municipality/id),
         data = df, control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")),
  `(1 | id)` =
    lmer(KamaMuta ~ Occasion * condition +
           (1 | id),
         data = df, control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")))

km_variances <- km_structures |>
  map(\(fit) as_tibble(VarCorr(fit))) |>
  list_rbind(names_to = "structure") |>
  summarise(smallest = min(vcov), .by = structure) |>
  mutate(above_zero = smallest >= 1e-8)

km_variances |>
  mutate(smallest = sprintf("%.1e", smallest))
structure smallest above_zero
(1 | trainedBy/Municipality/id) 2.9e-02 TRUE
(1 | Municipality/id) 1.0e-01 TRUE
(1 | id) 1.5e+00 TRUE 
# the first structure whose variances all lie above zero
km_richest <- km_variances$structure[km_variances$above_zero][1]

Do the groups really not differ? The two claims of absence, at baseline and after both trainings, with the preregistered and with the richest structure:

km_sd_T0 <- sd(df$KamaMuta[df$Occasion == "T0"], na.rm = TRUE)

km_tost <- bind_rows(
  preregistered = tidy(km_model, effects = "fixed"),
  richest       = tidy(km_structures[[km_richest]], effects = "fixed"),
  .id = "model") |>
  filter(term %in% c("conditionExperimental",
                     "OccasionT3:conditionExperimental")) |>
  transmute(model,
            claim   = if_else(term == "conditionExperimental", "baseline",
                              "after_both"),
            term,
            delta_d = estimate / km_sd_T0,
            se_d    = std.error / km_sd_T0,
            ci_low  = delta_d - qt(.95, df) * se_d,
            ci_high = delta_d + qt(.95, df) * se_d,
            p_tost  = pmax(pt((delta_d + sesoi) / se_d, df,
                              lower.tail = FALSE),
                           pt((delta_d - sesoi) / se_d, df)),
            p_two_sided = p.value,
            verdict = verdict_of(p_tost, p_two_sided))

km_tost |>
  select(model, claim, delta_d, ci_low, ci_high, p_tost, p_two_sided,
         verdict) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))
model claim delta_d ci_low ci_high p_tost p_two_sided verdict
preregistered baseline 0.092 -0.114 0.297 0.190 0.454 inconclusive
preregistered after_both -0.337 -0.558 -0.116 0.846 0.012 different
richest baseline 0.092 -0.106 0.291 0.180 0.429 inconclusive
richest after_both -0.334 -0.555 -0.113 0.841 0.013 different

Neither claim of absence can be shown. At baseline the test is inconclusive (Δd = 0.09, 90 % CI [-0.11, 0.30]). After both trainings the groups differ: the control group has gained more since January (Δd = -0.34, 90 % CI [-0.56, -0.12]). The richest structure with all variances above zero keeps the trainer level, persons in municipalities in trainers; it gives the same verdicts, and Δd moves by at most 0.003.

Next → Step 8, what follows: Where does the result go?

What follows · Step 8

Step 8 · What follows

Where does the result go? Kama Muta does not respond to the experimental group’s training, but the control group gains when it trains. Its interaction at T1 and its piecewise terms go to the comparison of the estimates in Chapter 20, its directional tests to the correction for many outcomes in 10.7.

Positivity Resonance

Step Question Result Next

5 Does the control group gain more while it trains? September to December: b = -0.42, p = .023; piecewise: b = -0.50, p = .004 random slopes

The model · Steps 1 and 2

Step 1 · The model both groups

Which model tests the training? The preregistered model:

res_model <- lmer(Resonance ~ Occasion * condition +
                    (1 | Municipality/id),
                  data = df)

res_fixed <- tidy(res_model, effects = "fixed") |>
  select(term, b = estimate, se = std.error, df, p = p.value)

res_fixed |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))
term b se df p
(Intercept) 7.404 0.099 923.271 0.000
OccasionT1 0.222 0.110 740.556 0.044
OccasionT2 0.304 0.112 826.249 0.007
OccasionT3 0.829 0.116 815.435 0.000
conditionExperimental -0.094 0.141 856.502 0.508
OccasionT1:conditionExperimental 0.384 0.154 735.984 0.013
OccasionT2:conditionExperimental 0.101 0.168 803.862 0.548
OccasionT3:conditionExperimental -0.239 0.186 787.179 0.198

In January the control group averages 7.40 on the scale from 0 to 10; the experimental group starts 0.09 points lower, a difference that is not significant (p = .508).

Does the model pass the textbook checks? Convergence, the same fixed effects with two other optimizers, no variance at zero, residuals and person intercepts close to normal, and the spread of the residuals over condition and wave:

res_checks <- lmm_checks(res_model)
res_checks
check value criterion holds
1 estimation: converged warning yes ✗
2 estimation: the same with bobyqa and Nelder-Mead converge, fixed effects within 0.0005 within .001 ✓
3 variances: none at zero smallest SD 0.003 (Municipality) not singular ✓
4 residuals: skewness -.59 within ±2 ✓
5 residuals: excess kurtosis 1.03 below 7 ✓
6 person intercepts: skewness -.53 within ±2 ✓
7 residuals: largest / smallest SD of the eight cells 1.28 reported – 
plot_residuals(res_model)

lme4 warns that its default optimizer stopped short of convergence. Bobyqa and Nelder-Mead fit the same model without a warning and agree with it on every fixed effect, to within 0.0005: the warning comes from the boundary, a variance close to zero (the SD between municipalities is 0.003), not from estimates that are off, and the model of step 1 stands.

Next → Step 2, the random structure: Is the municipality a level of its own?

Step 2 · The random structure both groups

Is the municipality a level of its own? The null model with persons nested in municipalities, against persons alone:

res_null_person <- lmer(Resonance ~ 1 + (1 | id),

AIC(res_null_person, res_null_nested) |>

res_null_nested 4 3765

res_shares |>

Municipality 0.003 0.001
Residual 0.993 0.500

res_trainer <- lmer(Resonance ~ Occasion * condition +
                      (1 | trainedBy/Municipality/id),
                    data = df,
                    control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa"))

AIC(res_model, res_trainer) |>
  mutate(AIC = round(AIC, 1))
df AIC
res_model 11 3710.4
res_trainer 12 3712.3

res_trainer_shares |>

level variance share

Municipality:trainedBy 0.000 0.000
trainedBy 0.005 0.003
Residual 0.899 0.473

AIC prefers persons alone, by 2.0 points: the municipalities take up only 0.1 % of the variance, against 49.8 % between the persons and 50.0 % between the questionnaires of a person. The municipality level stays nevertheless, as the conditions were assigned by municipality. The trainer level takes up 0.3 % of the variance but does not lower the AIC (it rises by 1.9 points). The model of step 1 stays.

bel_null_person <- lmer(Belongingness ~ 1 + (1 | id),
                        data = df)
bel_null_nested <- lmer(Belongingness ~ 1 + (1 | Municipality/id),
                        data = df)

AIC(bel_null_person, bel_null_nested) |>

bel_null_nested 4 4008.7

bel_shares |>

Municipality 0.035 0.014

bel_trainer <- lmer(Belongingness ~ Occasion * condition +
                      (1 | trainedBy/Municipality/id),
                    data = df,
                    control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa"))

AIC(bel_model, bel_trainer) |>
  mutate(AIC = round(AIC, 1))
df AIC
bel_model 11 3968.8
bel_trainer 12 3970.8

AIC prefers persons alone, by 1.0 points: the municipalities take up only 1.4 % of the variance, against 51.6 % between the persons and 47.0 % between the questionnaires of a person. The municipality level stays nevertheless, as the conditions were assigned by municipality. The trainer level takes up none of the variance and only adds a parameter: the AIC rises by 2.0 points. The model of step 1 stays.

Next → Step 3, the interactions: Does the experimental group change more?

The effects · Steps 3 to 5

Step 3 · The interactions both groups

Does the experimental group change more? The three interaction terms, with and without the trainer level:

bel_trainer_fixed <- tidy(bel_trainer, effects = "fixed") |>
  select(term, b_trainer = estimate, p_trainer = p.value)

bel_interactions <- bel_fixed |>
  filter(str_detect(term, ":")) |>
  left_join(bel_trainer_fixed, by = "term")

bel_interactions |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))
term b se df p b_trainer p_trainer
OccasionT1:conditionExperimental 0.306 0.168 709.581 0.070 0.306 0.070
OccasionT2:conditionExperimental 0.239 0.185 777.217 0.197 0.239 0.197
OccasionT3:conditionExperimental -0.373 0.204 754.384 0.068 -0.373 0.068

What does the model imply? The means of both groups at each wave; shaded the two training windows:

plot_means(bel_model)

By T1 the experimental group has not gained significantly more than the control group (b = 0.31, p = .070), nor by T2 (b = 0.24, p = .197). At T3, after the control group’s training, the groups do not differ significantly either (b = -0.37, p = .068). With the trainer level, the three terms stay the same to three decimals and keep their verdicts.

Next → Step 4, one-sided tests: Does it hold one-sided?

Step 4 · One-sided tests both groups

Does it hold one-sided? The effects at T1 and T2, where the hypotheses expect a positive sign:

bel_one_sided <- bel_interactions |>
  filter(term != "OccasionT3:conditionExperimental") |>
  transmute(term, b, p, p_one_sided = pt(b / se, df, lower.tail = FALSE))

bel_one_sided |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))
term b p p_one_sided
OccasionT1:conditionExperimental 0.306 0.070 0.035
OccasionT2:conditionExperimental 0.239 0.197 0.099

One-sided, the effect at T1 becomes significant (p = .035), the one at T2 non-significant (p = .099).

Next → Step 5, the replication: Does the control group gain when it trains?

Step 5 · The replication both groups

Does the control group gain when it trains? The period-specific model, on the September and December waves:

bel_period <- lmer(Belongingness ~ condition * Time_T3 +
                     (1 | Municipality/id),
                   data = df_T23)

bel_period_terms <- tidy(bel_period, effects = "fixed") |>
  filter(str_detect(term, ":")) |>
  transmute(term, b = estimate, se = std.error, df, p = p.value,
            singular = isSingular(bel_period))

bel_period_terms |>
  mutate(p_one_sided = pt(-b / se, df, lower.tail = FALSE),
         across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))
term b se df p singular p_one_sided
conditionExperimental:Time_T3 -0.628 0.191 213.17 0.001 FALSE 0.001

And over all four waves? The piecewise model, with one time indicator for each training:

bel_piecewise <- lmer(Belongingness ~ condition *
                        (Time_Exp_Training + Time_Control_Training) +
                        (1 | Municipality/id),
                      data = df)

bel_piecewise_terms <- tidy(bel_piecewise, effects = "fixed") |>
  filter(str_detect(term, ":")) |>
  transmute(term, b = estimate, se = std.error, df, p = p.value)

bel_piecewise_terms |>
  mutate(expected    = if_else(str_detect(term, "Time_Exp"), 1, -1),
         p_one_sided = pt(expected * b / se, df, lower.tail = FALSE),
         across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))
term b se df p expected p_one_sided
conditionExperimental:Time_Exp_Training 0.306 0.149 739.990 0.04 1 0.02
conditionExperimental:Time_Control_Training -0.689 0.188 723.012 0.00 -1 0.00

Between September and December, while the control group trains, it gains more than the experimental group (b = -0.63, p = .001). In the piecewise model the experimental group gains more while it trains (b = 0.31, p = .040), and the control group gains more while it trains (b = -0.69, p < .001).

Next → Step 6, random slopes: Does the change vary within each condition?

Robustness · Steps 6 and 7

Step 6 · Random slopes both groups

Does the change vary within each condition? The eight tests of the script (10.2), four in each condition:

bel_slopes_within <- slopes_within |>
  filter(outcome == "Belongingness") |>
  select(-outcome)

bel_slopes_within |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))
condition test chisq df p
Experimental slopes, municipalities 13.456 5 0.019
Experimental slope T0 vs. later, persons 26.392 2 0.000
Experimental slope T3 vs. earlier, persons 0.511 2 0.774
Experimental municipality x pre/post 10.682 9 0.298
Control slopes, municipalities 2.061 5 0.841
Control slope T0 vs. later, persons 15.745 2 0.000
Control slope T3 vs. earlier, persons 2.071 2 0.355

Three of the eight tests are significant: in the experimental group the slopes across municipalities and the slope of T0 against later across persons; in the control group the slope of T0 against later across persons. In neither condition do the municipalities gain differently from their own training.

Next → Step 7, equivalence: Which random structure is the richest?

Step 7 · Equivalence both groups

Which random structure is the richest? The model of step 1 under the three structures, fitted with bobyqa, and the smallest variance of each:

bel_structures <- list(
  `(1 | trainedBy/Municipality/id)` = bel_trainer,
  `(1 | Municipality/id)` =
    lmer(Belongingness ~ Occasion * condition +
           (1 | Municipality/id),
         data = df, control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")),
  `(1 | id)` =
    lmer(Belongingness ~ Occasion * condition +
           (1 | id),
         data = df, control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")))

bel_variances <- bel_structures |>
  map(\(fit) as_tibble(VarCorr(fit))) |>
  list_rbind(names_to = "structure") |>
  summarise(smallest = min(vcov), .by = structure) |>
  mutate(above_zero = smallest >= 1e-8)

bel_variances |>
  mutate(smallest = sprintf("%.1e", smallest))
structure smallest above_zero
(1 | trainedBy/Municipality/id) 0.0e+00 FALSE
(1 | Municipality/id) 3.5e-02 TRUE
(1 | id) 1.1e+00 TRUE 
# the first structure whose variances all lie above zero
bel_richest <- bel_variances$structure[bel_variances$above_zero][1]

Do the groups really not differ? The two claims of absence, at baseline and after both trainings, with the preregistered and with the richest structure:

bel_sd_T0 <- sd(df$Belongingness[df$Occasion == "T0"], na.rm = TRUE)

bel_tost <- bind_rows(
  preregistered = tidy(bel_model, effects = "fixed"),
  richest       = tidy(bel_structures[[bel_richest]], effects = "fixed"),
  .id = "model") |>
  filter(term %in% c("conditionExperimental",
                     "OccasionT3:conditionExperimental")) |>
  transmute(model,
            claim   = if_else(term == "conditionExperimental", "baseline",
                              "after_both"),
            term,
            delta_d = estimate / bel_sd_T0,
            se_d    = std.error / bel_sd_T0,
            ci_low  = delta_d - qt(.95, df) * se_d,
            ci_high = delta_d + qt(.95, df) * se_d,
            p_tost  = pmax(pt((delta_d + sesoi) / se_d, df,
                              lower.tail = FALSE),
                           pt((delta_d - sesoi) / se_d, df)),
            p_two_sided = p.value,
            verdict = verdict_of(p_tost, p_two_sided))

bel_tost |>
  select(model, claim, delta_d, ci_low, ci_high, p_tost, p_two_sided,
         verdict) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))
model claim delta_d ci_low ci_high p_tost p_two_sided verdict
preregistered baseline 0.021 -0.162 0.204 0.054 0.848 inconclusive
preregistered after_both -0.223 -0.424 -0.022 0.576 0.068 inconclusive
richest baseline 0.021 -0.162 0.204 0.054 0.848 inconclusive
richest after_both -0.223 -0.424 -0.022 0.576 0.068 inconclusive

Neither claim of absence can be shown. Both tests are inconclusive, as their intervals reach beyond ±0.20: at baseline Δd = 0.02, 90 % CI [-0.16, 0.20], after both trainings Δd = -0.22, 90 % CI [-0.42, -0.02]. The richest structure with all variances above zero is persons in municipalities, as in the preregistered model; it gives the same verdicts, and Δd stays the same to three decimals.

Next → Step 8, what follows: Where does the result go?

What follows · Step 8

Step 8 · What follows

Where does the result go? Belongingness misses significance at T1 two-sided but reaches it one-sided and in the piecewise model; the control group gains clearly when it trains. Its interaction at T1 and its piecewise terms go to the comparison of the estimates in Chapter 20, its directional tests to the correction for many outcomes in 10.7.

The model · Steps 1 and 2

Step 1 · The model both groups

Which model tests the training? The preregistered model:

nal_model <- lmer(NoAlienation ~ Occasion * condition +
                    (1 | Municipality/id),
                  data = df)

nal_fixed <- tidy(nal_model, effects = "fixed") |>
  select(term, b = estimate, se = std.error, df, p = p.value)

nal_fixed |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))
term b se df p
(Intercept) 4.598 0.290 31.873 0.000
OccasionT1 0.253 0.255 765.791 0.322
OccasionT2 -0.412 0.258 858.357 0.111
OccasionT3 -0.415 0.269 842.082 0.123
conditionExperimental 0.172 0.413 32.769 0.680
OccasionT1:conditionExperimental -0.758 0.356 764.616 0.033
OccasionT2:conditionExperimental 0.338 0.389 835.387 0.385
OccasionT3:conditionExperimental -0.038 0.430 813.826 0.930

In January the control group averages 4.60 on the scale from 0 to 10; the experimental group starts 0.17 points higher, a difference that is not significant (p = .680).

Does the model pass the textbook checks? Convergence, the same fixed effects with two other optimizers, no variance at zero, residuals and person intercepts close to normal, and the spread of the residuals over condition and wave:

nal_checks <- lmm_checks(nal_model)
nal_checks
check value criterion holds
1 estimation: converged yes yes ✓
2 estimation: the same with bobyqa and Nelder-Mead converge, fixed effects within 0.0000007 within .001 ✓
3 variances: none at zero smallest SD 0.592 (Municipality) not singular ✓

5 residuals: excess kurtosis .25 below 7 ✓
6 person intercepts: skewness .42 within ±2 ✓
7 residuals: largest / smallest SD of the eight cells 1.28 reported – 
plot_residuals(nal_model)

The model converges, two other optimizers give the same fixed effects, every variance lies above zero, and the residuals and the person intercepts stay within the bounds of normality; the residuals spread about evenly over condition and wave (the largest SD of a cell is 1.28 times the smallest).
