The model · Steps 1 and 2

Step 1 · The model both groups

Which model tests the training? The preregistered model:

nis_model <- lmer(NoIsolation ~ Occasion * condition +
                    (1 | Municipality/id),
                  data = df)

nis_fixed <- tidy(nis_model, effects = "fixed") |>
  select(term, b = estimate, se = std.error, df, p = p.value)

nis_fixed |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))
term b se df p
(Intercept) 2.839 0.273 33.889 0.000
OccasionT1 0.520 0.237 758.962 0.029
OccasionT2 0.419 0.241 844.072 0.082
OccasionT3 0.584 0.251 827.260 0.020
conditionExperimental 0.596 0.388 35.035 0.134
OccasionT1:conditionExperimental -0.333 0.331 757.220 0.314
OccasionT2:conditionExperimental -0.434 0.363 822.167 0.232
OccasionT3:conditionExperimental -0.442 0.400 800.244 0.270

In January the control group averages 2.84 on the scale from 0 to 10; the experimental group starts 0.60 points higher, a difference that is not significant (p = .134).

Does the model pass the textbook checks? Convergence, the same fixed effects with two other optimizers, no variance at zero, residuals and person intercepts close to normal, and the spread of the residuals over condition and wave:

nis_checks <- lmm_checks(nis_model)
nis_checks
check value criterion holds
1 estimation: converged yes yes ✓
2 estimation: the same with bobyqa and Nelder-Mead converge, fixed effects within 0.0000008 within .001 ✓
3 variances: none at zero smallest SD 0.539 (Municipality) not singular ✓
4 residuals: skewness .53 within ±2 ✓
5 residuals: excess kurtosis .78 below 7 ✓
6 person intercepts: skewness .66 within ±2 ✓
7 residuals: largest / smallest SD of the eight cells 1.30 reported – 
plot_residuals(nis_model)

The model converges, two other optimizers give the same fixed effects, every variance lies above zero, and the residuals and the person intercepts stay within the bounds of normality; the residuals spread about evenly over condition and wave (the largest SD of a cell is 1.30 times the smallest).

Next → Step 2, the random structure: Is the municipality a level of its own?

Step 2 · The random structure both groups

Is the municipality a level of its own? The null model with persons nested in municipalities, against persons alone:

nis_null_person <- lmer(NoIsolation ~ 1 + (1 | id),
                        data = df)
nis_null_nested <- lmer(NoIsolation ~ 1 + (1 | Municipality/id),
                        data = df)

AIC(nis_null_person, nis_null_nested) |>
  mutate(AIC = round(AIC, 1))
df AIC
nis_null_person 3 5451.8
nis_null_nested 4 5445.8

How is the variance shared? In the null model with both levels:

nis_shares <- as_tibble(VarCorr(nis_null_nested)) |>
  transmute(level = grp, variance = vcov, share = vcov / sum(vcov))

nis_shares |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))
level variance share
id:Municipality 4.452 0.499
Municipality 0.292 0.033
Residual 4.176 0.468

And the trainers? The model of step 1 with the trainers as a further level, and its variances:

nis_trainer <- lmer(NoIsolation ~ Occasion * condition +
                      (1 | trainedBy/Municipality/id),
                    data = df,
                    control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa"))

AIC(nis_model, nis_trainer) |>
  mutate(AIC = round(AIC, 1))
df AIC
nis_model 11 5457.4
nis_trainer 12 5459.2 
nis_trainer_shares <- as_tibble(VarCorr(nis_trainer)) |>
  transmute(level = grp, variance = vcov, share = vcov / sum(vcov))

nis_trainer_shares |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))
level variance share
id:Municipality:trainedBy 4.452 0.500
Municipality:trainedBy 0.221 0.025
trainedBy 0.071 0.008
Residual 4.166 0.468

AIC prefers persons nested in municipalities to persons alone, by 6.0 points. Of the variance, 3.3 % lies between the municipalities, 49.9 % between the persons of a municipality and 46.8 % between the questionnaires of a person. The trainer level takes up 0.8 % of the variance but does not lower the AIC (it rises by 1.9 points). With the default optimizer this model stops short of convergence; bobyqa reaches it. The model of step 1 stays.

Next → Step 3, the interactions: Does the experimental group change more?

The effects · Steps 3 to 5

Step 3 · The interactions both groups

Does the experimental group change more? The three interaction terms, with and without the trainer level:

nis_trainer_fixed <- tidy(nis_trainer, effects = "fixed") |>
  select(term, b_trainer = estimate, p_trainer = p.value)

nis_interactions <- nis_fixed |>
  filter(str_detect(term, ":")) |>
  left_join(nis_trainer_fixed, by = "term")

nis_interactions |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))
term b se df p b_trainer p_trainer
OccasionT1:conditionExperimental -0.333 0.331 757.220 0.314 -0.330 0.318
OccasionT2:conditionExperimental -0.434 0.363 822.167 0.232 -0.434 0.232
OccasionT3:conditionExperimental -0.442 0.400 800.244 0.270 -0.448 0.263

What does the model imply? The means of both groups at each wave; shaded the two training windows:

plot_means(nis_model)

By T1 the experimental group has not gained significantly more than the control group (b = -0.33, p = .314), nor by T2 (b = -0.43, p = .232). At T3, after the control group’s training, the groups do not differ significantly either (b = -0.44, p = .270). With the trainer level, the three terms move by at most 0.006 and keep their verdicts.

Next → Step 4, one-sided tests: Does it hold one-sided?

Step 4 · One-sided tests both groups

Does it hold one-sided? The effects at T1 and T2, where the hypotheses expect a positive sign:

nis_one_sided <- nis_interactions |>
  filter(term != "OccasionT3:conditionExperimental") |>
  transmute(term, b, p, p_one_sided = pt(b / se, df, lower.tail = FALSE))

nis_one_sided |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))
term b p p_one_sided
OccasionT1:conditionExperimental -0.333 0.314 0.843
OccasionT2:conditionExperimental -0.434 0.232 0.884

One-sided, both effects point against the expectation (p = .843 at T1, p = .884 at T2).

Next → Step 5, the replication: Does the control group gain when it trains?

Step 5 · The replication both groups

Does the control group gain when it trains? The period-specific model, on the September and December waves:

nis_period <- lmer(NoIsolation ~ condition * Time_T3 +
                     (1 | Municipality/id),
                   data = df_T23)

nis_period_terms <- tidy(nis_period, effects = "fixed") |>
  filter(str_detect(term, ":")) |>
  transmute(term, b = estimate, se = std.error, df, p = p.value,
            singular = isSingular(nis_period))

nis_period_terms |>
  mutate(p_one_sided = pt(-b / se, df, lower.tail = FALSE),
         across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))
term b se df p singular p_one_sided
conditionExperimental:Time_T3 -0.067 0.437 246.742 0.878 FALSE 0.439

And over all four waves? The piecewise model, with one time indicator for each training:

nis_piecewise <- lmer(NoIsolation ~ condition *
                        (Time_Exp_Training + Time_Control_Training) +
                        (1 | Municipality/id),
                      data = df)

nis_piecewise_terms <- tidy(nis_piecewise, effects = "fixed") |>
  filter(str_detect(term, ":")) |>
  transmute(term, b = estimate, se = std.error, df, p = p.value)

nis_piecewise_terms |>
  mutate(expected    = if_else(str_detect(term, "Time_Exp"), 1, -1),
         p_one_sided = pt(expected * b / se, df, lower.tail = FALSE),
         across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))
term b se df p expected p_one_sided
conditionExperimental:Time_Exp_Training -0.357 0.290 786.846 0.218 1 0.891
conditionExperimental:Time_Control_Training -0.086 0.367 769.490 0.814 -1 0.407

Between September and December, while the control group trains, it does not gain significantly more than the experimental group (b = -0.07, p = .878). In the piecewise model the experimental group’s training window shows no significant effect (b = -0.36, p = .218), and the control group’s window shows none either (b = -0.09, p = .814).

Next → Step 6, random slopes: Does the change vary within each condition?

Robustness · Steps 6 and 7

Step 6 · Random slopes both groups

Does the change vary within each condition? The eight tests of the script (10.2), four in each condition:

nis_slopes_within <- slopes_within |>
  filter(outcome == "NoIsolation") |>
  select(-outcome)

nis_slopes_within |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))
condition test chisq df p
Experimental slopes, municipalities 0.432 5 0.994
Experimental slope T0 vs. later, persons 1.246 2 0.536
Experimental slope T3 vs. earlier, persons 5.155 2 0.076
Experimental municipality x pre/post 4.711 9 0.859
Control slopes, municipalities 2.387 5 0.793
Control slope T0 vs. later, persons 1.301 2 0.522
Control slope T3 vs. earlier, persons 3.667 2 0.160
Control municipality x pre/post 8.213 9 0.513

None of the eight tests is significant: within each condition the change varies neither between the municipalities nor between the persons.

Next → Step 7, equivalence: Which random structure is the richest?

Step 7 · Equivalence both groups

Which random structure is the richest? The model of step 1 under the three structures, fitted with bobyqa, and the smallest variance of each:

nis_structures <- list(
  `(1 | trainedBy/Municipality/id)` = nis_trainer,
  `(1 | Municipality/id)` =
    lmer(NoIsolation ~ Occasion * condition +
           (1 | Municipality/id),
         data = df, control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")),
  `(1 | id)` =
    lmer(NoIsolation ~ Occasion * condition +
           (1 | id),
         data = df, control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")))

nis_variances <- nis_structures |>
  map(\(fit) as_tibble(VarCorr(fit))) |>
  list_rbind(names_to = "structure") |>
  summarise(smallest = min(vcov), .by = structure) |>
  mutate(above_zero = smallest >= 1e-8)

nis_variances |>
  mutate(smallest = sprintf("%.1e", smallest))
structure smallest above_zero
(1 | trainedBy/Municipality/id) 7.1e-02 TRUE
(1 | Municipality/id) 2.9e-01 TRUE
(1 | id) 4.2e+00 TRUE 
# the first structure whose variances all lie above zero
nis_richest <- nis_variances$structure[nis_variances$above_zero][1]

Do the groups really not differ? The two claims of absence, at baseline and after both trainings, with the preregistered and with the richest structure:

nis_sd_T0 <- sd(df$NoIsolation[df$Occasion == "T0"], na.rm = TRUE)

nis_tost <- bind_rows(
  preregistered = tidy(nis_model, effects = "fixed"),
  richest       = tidy(nis_structures[[nis_richest]], effects = "fixed"),
  .id = "model") |>
  filter(term %in% c("conditionExperimental",
                     "OccasionT3:conditionExperimental")) |>
  transmute(model,
            claim   = if_else(term == "conditionExperimental", "baseline",
                              "after_both"),
            term,
            delta_d = estimate / nis_sd_T0,
            se_d    = std.error / nis_sd_T0,
            ci_low  = delta_d - qt(.95, df) * se_d,
            ci_high = delta_d + qt(.95, df) * se_d,
            p_tost  = pmax(pt((delta_d + sesoi) / se_d, df,
                              lower.tail = FALSE),
                           pt((delta_d - sesoi) / se_d, df)),
            p_two_sided = p.value,
            verdict = verdict_of(p_tost, p_two_sided))

nis_tost |>
  select(model, claim, delta_d, ci_low, ci_high, p_tost, p_two_sided,
         verdict) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))
model claim delta_d ci_low ci_high p_tost p_two_sided verdict
preregistered baseline 0.200 -0.020 0.419 0.499 0.134 inconclusive
preregistered after_both -0.148 -0.369 0.073 0.349 0.270 inconclusive
richest baseline 0.200 -0.016 0.415 0.498 0.125 inconclusive
richest after_both -0.150 -0.371 0.071 0.355 0.263 inconclusive

Neither claim of absence can be shown. Both tests are inconclusive, as their intervals reach beyond ±0.20: at baseline Δd = 0.20, 90 % CI [-0.02, 0.42], after both trainings Δd = -0.15, 90 % CI [-0.37, 0.07]. The richest structure with all variances above zero keeps the trainer level, persons in municipalities in trainers; it gives the same verdicts, and Δd moves by at most 0.002.

Next → Step 8, what follows: Where does the result go?

What follows · Step 8

Step 8 · What follows

Where does the result go? No Isolation shows no training effect in any model. Its interaction at T1 and its piecewise terms go to the comparison of the estimates in Chapter 20, its directional tests to the correction for many outcomes in 10.7.

10.4 Cognitive complexity (H2)

Rogerian Schema

Its path through the steps. One row per step below, from the models of the steps, fitted once more; every step uses both groups both groups:

Step Question Result Next
1 Does the model pass the textbook checks? yes, all six random structure
2 Municipalities a level of their own? Trainers? municipalities: not by AIC, kept by design; trainers: no interactions
3 Does the experimental group change more (T1, T2, T3)? T1: b = 0.38, p = .005; T2: b = 0.16, p = .274; T3: b = 0.13, p = .418 one-sided tests
5 Does the control group gain more while it trains? September to December: b = -0.12, p = .467; piecewise: b = -0.15, p = .321 random slopes
6 Does the change vary within a condition? 0 of 8 tests significant equivalence
7 Alike at baseline and after both trainings (TOST)? baseline: inconclusive; after both: inconclusive what follows
8 Where next? Chapter 20; 10.7

What follows · Step 8

Step 8 · What follows

Where does the result go? Rogerian Schema shows the training effect at T1 and in the experimental group’s window of the piecewise model, but the control group does not gain more when it trains. Its interaction at T1 and its piecewise terms go to the comparison of the estimates in Chapter 20, its directional tests to the correction for many outcomes in 10.7.

Next → Step 7, equivalence: Which random structure is the richest?

Step 7 · Equivalence both groups

Which random structure is the richest? The model of step 1 under the three structures, fitted with bobyqa, and the smallest variance of each:

pm_structures <- list(
  `(1 | trainedBy/Municipality/id)` = pm_trainer,
  `(1 | Municipality/id)` =
    lmer(ParadoxMindset ~ Occasion * condition +
           (1 | Municipality/id),
         data = df, control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")),
  `(1 | id)` =
    lmer(ParadoxMindset ~ Occasion * condition +
           (1 | id),
         data = df, control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")))

pm_variances <- pm_structures |>
  map(\(fit) as_tibble(VarCorr(fit))) |>
  list_rbind(names_to = "structure") |>
  summarise(smallest = min(vcov), .by = structure) |>
  mutate(above_zero = smallest >= 1e-8)

pm_variances |>
  mutate(smallest = sprintf("%.1e", smallest))
structure smallest above_zero
(1 | trainedBy/Municipality/id) 4.1e-14 FALSE
(1 | Municipality/id) 9.1e-02 TRUE
(1 | id) 1.4e+00 TRUE 
# the first structure whose variances all lie above zero
pm_richest <- pm_variances$structure[pm_variances$above_zero][1]

Do the groups really not differ? The two claims of absence, at baseline and after both trainings, with the preregistered and with the richest structure:

pm_sd_T0 <- sd(df$ParadoxMindset[df$Occasion == "T0"], na.rm = TRUE)

pm_tost <- bind_rows(
  preregistered = tidy(pm_model, effects = "fixed"),
  richest       = tidy(pm_structures[[pm_richest]], effects = "fixed"),
  .id = "model") |>
  filter(term %in% c("conditionExperimental",
                     "OccasionT3:conditionExperimental")) |>
  transmute(model,
            claim   = if_else(term == "conditionExperimental", "baseline",
                              "after_both"),
            term,
            delta_d = estimate / pm_sd_T0,
            se_d    = std.error / pm_sd_T0,
            ci_low  = delta_d - qt(.95, df) * se_d,
            ci_high = delta_d + qt(.95, df) * se_d,
            p_tost  = pmax(pt((delta_d + sesoi) / se_d, df,
                              lower.tail = FALSE),
                           pt((delta_d - sesoi) / se_d, df)),
            p_two_sided = p.value,
            verdict = verdict_of(p_tost, p_two_sided))

pm_tost |>
  select(model, claim, delta_d, ci_low, ci_high, p_tost, p_two_sided,
         verdict) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))
model claim delta_d ci_low ci_high p_tost p_two_sided verdict
preregistered baseline -0.034 -0.240 0.171 0.091 0.779 inconclusive
preregistered after_both -0.191 -0.397 0.015 0.471 0.127 inconclusive
richest baseline -0.034 -0.240 0.171 0.091 0.779 inconclusive
richest after_both -0.191 -0.397 0.015 0.471 0.127 inconclusive

Neither claim of absence can be shown. Both tests are inconclusive, as their intervals reach beyond ±0.20: at baseline Δd = -0.03, 90 % CI [-0.24, 0.17], after both trainings Δd = -0.19, 90 % CI [-0.40, 0.01]. The richest structure with all variances above zero is persons in municipalities, as in the preregistered model; it gives the same verdicts, and Δd stays the same to three decimals.

         data = df, control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")))

ih_variances <- ih_structures |>
  map(\(fit) as_tibble(VarCorr(fit))) |>
  list_rbind(names_to = "structure") |>
  summarise(smallest = min(vcov), .by = structure) |>
  mutate(above_zero = smallest >= 1e-8)

ih_variances |>
  mutate(smallest = sprintf("%.1e", smallest))
structure smallest above_zero
(1 | trainedBy/Municipality/id) 0.0e+00 FALSE
(1 | Municipality/id) 5.8e-02 TRUE
(1 | id) 7.8e-01 TRUE 
# the first structure whose variances all lie above zero
ih_richest <- ih_variances$structure[ih_variances$above_zero][1]

Do the groups really not differ? The two claims of absence, at baseline and after both trainings, with the preregistered and with the richest structure:

ih_sd_T0 <- sd(df$IntellectualHumility[df$Occasion == "T0"], na.rm = TRUE)

ih_tost <- bind_rows(
  preregistered = tidy(ih_model, effects = "fixed"),
  richest       = tidy(ih_structures[[ih_richest]], effects = "fixed"),
  .id = "model") |>
  filter(term %in% c("conditionExperimental",
                     "OccasionT3:conditionExperimental")) |>
  transmute(model,
            claim   = if_else(term == "conditionExperimental", "baseline",
                              "after_both"),
            term,
            delta_d = estimate / ih_sd_T0,
            se_d    = std.error / ih_sd_T0,
            ci_low  = delta_d - qt(.95, df) * se_d,
            ci_high = delta_d + qt(.95, df) * se_d,
            p_tost  = pmax(pt((delta_d + sesoi) / se_d, df,
                              lower.tail = FALSE),
                           pt((delta_d - sesoi) / se_d, df)),
            p_two_sided = p.value,
            verdict = verdict_of(p_tost, p_two_sided))

ih_tost |>
  select(model, claim, delta_d, ci_low, ci_high, p_tost, p_two_sided,
         verdict) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))
model claim delta_d ci_low ci_high p_tost p_two_sided verdict
preregistered baseline 0.038 -0.179 0.256 0.108 0.768 inconclusive
preregistered after_both -0.307 -0.528 -0.086 0.787 0.023 different
richest baseline 0.038 -0.179 0.256 0.108 0.768 inconclusive
richest after_both -0.307 -0.528 -0.086 0.787 0.023 different

Neither claim of absence can be shown. At baseline the test is inconclusive (Δd = 0.04, 90 % CI [-0.18, 0.26]). After both trainings the groups differ: the control group has gained more since January (Δd = -0.31, 90 % CI [-0.53, -0.09]). The richest structure with all variances above zero is persons in municipalities, as in the preregistered model; it gives the same verdicts, and Δd stays the same to three decimals.

What follows · Step 8

Step 8 · What follows

Where does the result go? Intellectual Humility does not respond to the experimental group’s training; after both trainings the control group has gained more since January. Its interaction at T1 and its piecewise terms go to the comparison of the estimates in Chapter 20, its directional tests to the correction for many outcomes in 10.7.

Step 3 · The interactions both groups

Does the experimental group change more? The three interaction terms, with and without the trainer level:

What does the model imply? The means of both groups at each wave; shaded the two training windows:

plot_means(td_model)

By T1 the experimental group has not gained significantly more than the control group (b = -0.04, p = .818), nor by T2 (b = -0.17, p = .404). At T3, after the control group’s training, the groups do not differ significantly either (b = -0.30, p = .184). With the trainer level, the three terms move by at most 0.004 and keep their verdicts.

Next → Step 5, the replication: Does the control group gain when it trains?

Step 5 · The replication both groups

Does the control group gain when it trains? The period-specific model, on the September and December waves:

td_period <- lmer(ToleranceDiversity ~ condition * Time_T3 +
                    (1 | Municipality/id),
                  data = df_T23)

td_period_terms <- tidy(td_period, effects = "fixed") |>
  filter(str_detect(term, ":")) |>
  transmute(term, b = estimate, se = std.error, df, p = p.value,
            singular = isSingular(td_period))

td_period_terms |>
  mutate(p_one_sided = pt(-b / se, df, lower.tail = FALSE),
         across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))
term b se df p singular p_one_sided
conditionExperimental:Time_T3 -0.233 0.237 233.15 0.327 FALSE 0.164

And over all four waves? The piecewise model, with one time indicator for each training:

td_piecewise <- lmer(ToleranceDiversity ~ condition *
                       (Time_Exp_Training + Time_Control_Training) +
                       (1 | Municipality/id),
                     data = df)

td_piecewise_terms <- tidy(td_piecewise, effects = "fixed") |>
  filter(str_detect(term, ":")) |>
  transmute(term, b = estimate, se = std.error, df, p = p.value)

td_piecewise_terms |>
  mutate(expected    = if_else(str_detect(term, "Time_Exp"), 1, -1),
         p_one_sided = pt(expected * b / se, df, lower.tail = FALSE),
         across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))
term b se df p expected p_one_sided
conditionExperimental:Time_Exp_Training -0.109 0.165 766.726 0.510 1 0.745
conditionExperimental:Time_Control_Training -0.181 0.209 750.691 0.386 -1 0.193

Between September and December, while the control group trains, it does not gain significantly more than the experimental group (b = -0.23, p = .327). In the piecewise model the experimental group’s training window shows no significant effect (b = -0.11, p = .510), and the control group’s window shows none either (b = -0.18, p = .386).

Next → Step 7, equivalence: Which random structure is the richest?

Step 7 · Equivalence both groups

Which random structure is the richest? The model of step 1 under the three structures, fitted with bobyqa, and the smallest variance of each:

wa_structures <- list(
  `(1 | trainedBy/Municipality/id)` = wa_trainer,
  `(1 | Municipality/id)` =
    lmer(womenAttitude ~ Occasion * condition +
           (1 | Municipality/id),
         data = df, control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")),
  `(1 | id)` =
    lmer(womenAttitude ~ Occasion * condition +
           (1 | id),
         data = df, control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")))

wa_variances <- wa_structures |>
  map(\(fit) as_tibble(VarCorr(fit))) |>
  list_rbind(names_to = "structure") |>
  summarise(smallest = min(vcov), .by = structure) |>
  mutate(above_zero = smallest >= 1e-8)

wa_variances |>
  mutate(smallest = sprintf("%.1e", smallest))
structure smallest above_zero
(1 | trainedBy/Municipality/id) 0.0e+00 FALSE
(1 | Municipality/id) 1.6e-02 TRUE
(1 | id) 3.3e-01 TRUE 
# the first structure whose variances all lie above zero
wa_richest <- wa_variances$structure[wa_variances$above_zero][1]

Do the groups really not differ? The two claims of absence, at baseline and after both trainings, with the preregistered and with the richest structure:

wa_sd_T0 <- sd(df$womenAttitude[df$Occasion == "T0"], na.rm = TRUE)

wa_tost <- bind_rows(
  preregistered = tidy(wa_model, effects = "fixed"),
  richest       = tidy(wa_structures[[wa_richest]], effects = "fixed"),
  .id = "model") |>
  filter(term %in% c("conditionExperimental",
                     "OccasionT3:conditionExperimental")) |>
  transmute(model,
            claim   = if_else(term == "conditionExperimental", "baseline",
                              "after_both"),
            term,
            delta_d = estimate / wa_sd_T0,
            se_d    = std.error / wa_sd_T0,
            ci_low  = delta_d - qt(.95, df) * se_d,
            ci_high = delta_d + qt(.95, df) * se_d,
            p_tost  = pmax(pt((delta_d + sesoi) / se_d, df,
                              lower.tail = FALSE),
                           pt((delta_d - sesoi) / se_d, df)),
            p_two_sided = p.value,
            verdict = verdict_of(p_tost, p_two_sided))

wa_tost |>
  select(model, claim, delta_d, ci_low, ci_high, p_tost, p_two_sided,
         verdict) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))
model claim delta_d ci_low ci_high p_tost p_two_sided verdict
preregistered baseline -0.130 -0.329 0.069 0.278 0.277 inconclusive
preregistered after_both 0.023 -0.212 0.258 0.107 0.873 inconclusive
richest baseline -0.130 -0.329 0.069 0.278 0.277 inconclusive
richest after_both 0.023 -0.212 0.258 0.107 0.873 inconclusive

Neither claim of absence can be shown. Both tests are inconclusive, as their intervals reach beyond ±0.20: at baseline Δd = -0.13, 90 % CI [-0.33, 0.07], after both trainings Δd = 0.02, 90 % CI [-0.21, 0.26]. The richest structure with all variances above zero is persons in municipalities, as in the preregistered model; it gives the same verdicts, and Δd stays the same to three decimals.

Next → Step 8, what follows: Where does the result go?

What follows · Step 8

Step 8 · What follows

Where does the result go? Women Attitude shows a small effect at T1 that neither the piecewise model nor the replication repeats. Its interaction at T1 and its piecewise terms go to the comparison of the estimates in Chapter 20, its directional tests to the correction for many outcomes in 10.7.

The model · Steps 1 and 2

Step 1 · The model both groups

Which model tests the training? The preregistered model:

The model converges, two other optimizers give the same fixed effects, every variance lies above zero, and the residuals and the person intercepts stay within the bounds of normality; the residuals spread about evenly over condition and wave (the largest SD of a cell is 1.14 times the smallest).

Next → Step 2, the random structure: Is the municipality a level of its own?

Is the municipality a level of its own? The null model with persons nested in municipalities, against persons alone:

                   control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa"))

AIC(fl_model, fl_trainer) |>

df AIC

AIC prefers persons nested in municipalities to persons alone, by 2.2 points. Of the variance, 2.4 % lies between the municipalities, 52.8 % between the persons of a municipality and 44.8 % between the questionnaires of a person. The trainer level takes up 2.3 % of the variance and lowers the AIC slightly, by 1.0 points. The gain is too small to prefer the trainer level, and step 3 shows that the interaction terms hardly move with it: the model of step 1 stays.

Step 3 · The interactions both groups

Does the experimental group change more? The three interaction terms, with and without the trainer level:

  select(term, b_trainer = estimate, p_trainer = p.value)

What does the model imply? The means of both groups at each wave; shaded the two training windows:

plot_means(fl_model)

By T1 the experimental group has not gained significantly more than the control group (b = 0.15, p = .343), nor by T2 (b = 0.10, p = .552). At T3, after the control group’s training, the groups do not differ significantly either (b = -0.12, p = .521). With the trainer level, the three terms move by at most 0.005 and keep their verdicts.

Does it hold one-sided? The effects at T1 and T2, where the hypotheses expect a positive sign:

asat_one_sided <- asat_interactions |>
  filter(term != "OccasionT3:conditionExperimental") |>
  transmute(term, b, p, p_one_sided = pt(b / se, df, lower.tail = FALSE))

asat_one_sided |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))
term b p p_one_sided
OccasionT1:conditionExperimental 0.318 0.03 0.015
OccasionT2:conditionExperimental 0.024 0.88 0.440

One-sided, the effect at T1 remains significant (p = .015), the one at T2 non-significant (p = .440).

Next → Step 5, the replication: Does the control group gain when it trains?

Step 5 · The replication both groups

Does the control group gain when it trains? The period-specific model, on the September and December waves:

asat_period <- lmer(AutonomySatisfaction ~ condition * Time_T3 +
                      (1 | Municipality/id),
                    data = df_T23)

asat_period_terms <- tidy(asat_period, effects = "fixed") |>
  filter(str_detect(term, ":")) |>
  transmute(term, b = estimate, se = std.error, df, p = p.value,
            singular = isSingular(asat_period))

asat_period_terms |>
  mutate(p_one_sided = pt(-b / se, df, lower.tail = FALSE),
         across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))
term b se df p singular p_one_sided
conditionExperimental:Time_T3 -0.279 0.164 208.99 0.09 FALSE 0.045

And over all four waves? The piecewise model, with one time indicator for each training:

asat_piecewise <- lmer(AutonomySatisfaction ~ condition *
                         (Time_Exp_Training + Time_Control_Training) +
                         (1 | Municipality/id),
                       data = df)

asat_piecewise_terms <- tidy(asat_piecewise, effects = "fixed") |>
  filter(str_detect(term, ":")) |>
  transmute(term, b = estimate, se = std.error, df, p = p.value)

asat_piecewise_terms |>
  mutate(expected    = if_else(str_detect(term, "Time_Exp"), 1, -1),
         p_one_sided = pt(expected * b / se, df, lower.tail = FALSE),
         across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))
term b se df p expected p_one_sided
conditionExperimental:Time_Exp_Training 0.192 0.129 765.366 0.137 1 0.068
conditionExperimental:Time_Control_Training -0.295 0.163 748.438 0.070 -1 0.035

Between September and December, while the control group trains, it does not gain significantly more than the experimental group (b = -0.28, p = .090). In the piecewise model the experimental group’s training window shows no significant effect (b = 0.19, p = .137), and the control group’s window shows none either (b = -0.30, p = .070).

Step 6 · Random slopes both groups

Does the change vary within each condition? The eight tests of the script (10.2), four in each condition:

asat_slopes_within <- slopes_within |>
  filter(outcome == "AutonomySatisfaction") |>
  select(-outcome)

asat_slopes_within |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))
condition test chisq df p

Two of the eight tests are significant: the slope of T0 against later across persons in both groups. In neither condition do the municipalities gain differently from their own training.

Next → Step 7, equivalence: Which random structure is the richest?

Step 7 · Equivalence both groups

Which random structure is the richest? The model of step 1 under the three structures, fitted with bobyqa, and the smallest variance of each:

asat_structures <- list(
  `(1 | trainedBy/Municipality/id)` = asat_trainer,
  `(1 | Municipality/id)` =
    lmer(AutonomySatisfaction ~ Occasion * condition +
           (1 | Municipality/id),
         data = df, control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")),
  `(1 | id)` =
    lmer(AutonomySatisfaction ~ Occasion * condition +
           (1 | id),
         data = df, control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")))

asat_variances <- asat_structures |>
  map(\(fit) as_tibble(VarCorr(fit))) |>
  list_rbind(names_to = "structure") |>
  summarise(smallest = min(vcov), .by = structure) |>
  mutate(above_zero = smallest >= 1e-8)

asat_variances |>
  mutate(smallest = sprintf("%.1e", smallest))
structure smallest above_zero
(1 | trainedBy/Municipality/id) 8.6e-03 TRUE
(1 | Municipality/id) 2.9e-02 TRUE
(1 | id) 8.1e-01 TRUE 
# the first structure whose variances all lie above zero
asat_richest <- asat_variances$structure[asat_variances$above_zero][1]

Do the groups really not differ? The two claims of absence, at baseline and after both trainings, with the preregistered and with the richest structure:

asat_sd_T0 <- sd(df$AutonomySatisfaction[df$Occasion == "T0"], na.rm = TRUE)

asat_tost <- bind_rows(
  preregistered = tidy(asat_model, effects = "fixed"),
  richest       = tidy(asat_structures[[asat_richest]], effects = "fixed"),
  .id = "model") |>
  filter(term %in% c("conditionExperimental",
                     "OccasionT3:conditionExperimental")) |>
  transmute(model,
            claim   = if_else(term == "conditionExperimental", "baseline",
                              "after_both"),
            term,
            delta_d = estimate / asat_sd_T0,
            se_d    = std.error / asat_sd_T0,
            ci_low  = delta_d - qt(.95, df) * se_d,
            ci_high = delta_d + qt(.95, df) * se_d,
            p_tost  = pmax(pt((delta_d + sesoi) / se_d, df,
                              lower.tail = FALSE),
                           pt((delta_d - sesoi) / se_d, df)),
            p_two_sided = p.value,
            verdict = verdict_of(p_tost, p_two_sided))

asat_tost |>
  select(model, claim, delta_d, ci_low, ci_high, p_tost, p_two_sided,
         verdict) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))
model claim delta_d ci_low ci_high p_tost p_two_sided verdict
preregistered baseline -0.208 -0.394 -0.021 0.527 0.069 inconclusive
preregistered after_both -0.085 -0.288 0.117 0.175 0.489 inconclusive
richest baseline -0.205 -0.379 -0.031 0.521 0.055 inconclusive
richest after_both -0.080 -0.282 0.123 0.164 0.516 inconclusive

Neither claim of absence can be shown. Both tests are inconclusive, as their intervals reach beyond ±0.20: at baseline Δd = -0.21, 90 % CI [-0.39, -0.02], after both trainings Δd = -0.09, 90 % CI [-0.29, 0.12]. The richest structure with all variances above zero keeps the trainer level, persons in municipalities in trainers; it gives the same verdicts, and Δd moves by at most 0.005.

Next → Step 8, what follows: Where does the result go?

What follows · Step 8

Step 8 · What follows

Where does the result go? Autonomy Satisfaction shows the training effect at T1 only; neither the piecewise model nor the replication repeats it. Its interaction at T1 and its piecewise terms go to the comparison of the estimates in Chapter 20, its directional tests to the correction for many outcomes in 10.7.

Relatedness Satisfaction

5 Does the control group gain more while it trains? September to December: b = -0.34, p = .010; piecewise: b = -0.37, p = .002 random slopes
6 Does the change vary within a condition? 1 of 8 tests significant equivalence

The model · Steps 1 and 2

Step 1 · The model both groups

Which model tests the training? The preregistered model:

rsat_model <- lmer(RelatednessSatisfaction ~ Occasion * condition +
                     (1 | Municipality/id),
                   data = df)

rsat_fixed <- tidy(rsat_model, effects = "fixed") |>
  select(term, b = estimate, se = std.error, df, p = p.value)

rsat_fixed |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))
term b se df p
(Intercept) 9.028 0.069 893.452 0.000
OccasionT1 -0.015 0.075 724.367 0.845
OccasionT2 -0.005 0.077 814.103 0.952
OccasionT3 0.298 0.080 798.199 0.000
conditionExperimental 0.092 0.099 823.290 0.352
OccasionT1:conditionExperimental 0.212 0.105 722.037 0.044
OccasionT2:conditionExperimental 0.007 0.115 790.507 0.954
OccasionT3:conditionExperimental -0.238 0.127 771.165 0.061

In January the control group averages 9.03 on the scale from 0 to 10; the experimental group starts 0.09 points higher, a difference that is not significant (p = .352).

Does the model pass the textbook checks? Convergence, the same fixed effects with two other optimizers, no variance at zero, residuals and person intercepts close to normal, and the spread of the residuals over condition and wave:

rsat_checks <- lmm_checks(rsat_model)
rsat_checks
check value criterion holds
1 estimation: converged yes yes ✓
2 estimation: the same with bobyqa and Nelder-Mead converge, fixed effects within 0.0000001 within .001 ✓
3 variances: none at zero smallest SD 0.000 (Municipality) not singular ✗
4 residuals: skewness -1.09 within ±2 ✓
5 residuals: excess kurtosis 2.89 below 7 ✓
6 person intercepts: skewness -1.22 within ±2 ✓
7 residuals: largest / smallest SD of the eight cells 1.50 reported – 
plot_residuals(rsat_model)

A variance is estimated at zero, between municipalities: the model reduces to a simpler random structure, which leaves the fixed effects as they are; step 7 repeats the claims of absence with the richest structure whose variances all lie above zero.

Next → Step 2, the random structure: Is the municipality a level of its own?

Is the municipality a level of its own? The null model with persons nested in municipalities, against persons alone:

AIC(rsat_model, rsat_trainer) |>

df AIC
rsat_model 11 2901.9
rsat_trainer 12 2903.9

level variance share

Municipality:trainedBy 0.000 0.000
trainedBy 0.000 0.000
Residual 0.419 0.444

AIC prefers persons alone, by 2.0 points: almost none of the variance lies between the municipalities, against 55.0 % between the persons and 45.0 % between the questionnaires of a person. The municipality level stays nevertheless, as the conditions were assigned by municipality. The trainer level takes up almost none of the variance and does not lower the AIC (it rises by 2.0 points). With the default optimizer this model stops short of convergence; bobyqa reaches it. The model of step 1 stays.

Next → Step 3, the interactions: Does the experimental group change more?

Step 3 · The interactions both groups

Does the experimental group change more? The three interaction terms, with and without the trainer level:

  select(term, b_trainer = estimate, p_trainer = p.value)

  left_join(rsat_trainer_fixed, by = "term")

OccasionT3:conditionExperimental -0.238 0.127 771.165 0.061 -0.238 0.061

What does the model imply? The means of both groups at each wave; shaded the two training windows:

plot_means(rsat_model)

By T1 the experimental group has gained more than the control group (b = 0.21, p = .044); by T2 the advantage has faded (b = 0.01, p = .954). At T3, after the control group’s training, the change since January no longer differs significantly (b = -0.24, p = .061). With the trainer level, the three terms stay the same to three decimals and keep their verdicts.

Next → Step 7, equivalence: Which random structure is the richest?

Step 7 · Equivalence both groups

Which random structure is the richest? The model of step 1 under the three structures, fitted with bobyqa, and the smallest variance of each:

csat_structures <- list(
  `(1 | trainedBy/Municipality/id)` = csat_trainer,
  `(1 | Municipality/id)` =
    lmer(CompetenceSatisfaction ~ Occasion * condition +
           (1 | Municipality/id),
         data = df, control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")),
  `(1 | id)` =
    lmer(CompetenceSatisfaction ~ Occasion * condition +
           (1 | id),
         data = df, control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")))

csat_variances <- csat_structures |>
  map(\(fit) as_tibble(VarCorr(fit))) |>
  list_rbind(names_to = "structure") |>
  summarise(smallest = min(vcov), .by = structure) |>
  mutate(above_zero = smallest >= 1e-8)

csat_variances |>
  mutate(smallest = sprintf("%.1e", smallest))
structure smallest above_zero
(1 | trainedBy/Municipality/id) 0.0e+00 FALSE
(1 | Municipality/id) 3.9e-02 TRUE
(1 | id) 4.5e-01 TRUE 
# the first structure whose variances all lie above zero
csat_richest <- csat_variances$structure[csat_variances$above_zero][1]

Do the groups really not differ? The two claims of absence, at baseline and after both trainings, with the preregistered and with the richest structure:

csat_sd_T0 <- sd(df$CompetenceSatisfaction[df$Occasion == "T0"], na.rm = TRUE)

csat_tost <- bind_rows(
  preregistered = tidy(csat_model, effects = "fixed"),
  richest       = tidy(csat_structures[[csat_richest]], effects = "fixed"),
  .id = "model") |>
  filter(term %in% c("conditionExperimental",
                     "OccasionT3:conditionExperimental")) |>
  transmute(model,
            claim   = if_else(term == "conditionExperimental", "baseline",
                              "after_both"),
            term,
            delta_d = estimate / csat_sd_T0,
            se_d    = std.error / csat_sd_T0,
            ci_low  = delta_d - qt(.95, df) * se_d,
            ci_high = delta_d + qt(.95, df) * se_d,
            p_tost  = pmax(pt((delta_d + sesoi) / se_d, df,
                              lower.tail = FALSE),
                           pt((delta_d - sesoi) / se_d, df)),
            p_two_sided = p.value,
            verdict = verdict_of(p_tost, p_two_sided))

csat_tost |>
  select(model, claim, delta_d, ci_low, ci_high, p_tost, p_two_sided,
         verdict) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))
model claim delta_d ci_low ci_high p_tost p_two_sided verdict
preregistered baseline -0.31 -0.510 -0.11 0.822 0.014 different
preregistered after_both 0.03 -0.149 0.21 0.060 0.782 inconclusive
richest baseline -0.31 -0.510 -0.11 0.822 0.014 different
richest after_both 0.03 -0.149 0.21 0.060 0.782 inconclusive

Neither claim of absence can be shown. At baseline the groups differ: the experimental group starts lower (Δd = -0.31, 90 % CI [-0.51, -0.11]). After both trainings the test is inconclusive (Δd = 0.03, 90 % CI [-0.15, 0.21]). The richest structure with all variances above zero is persons in municipalities, as in the preregistered model; it gives the same verdicts, and Δd stays the same to three decimals.

The model · Steps 1 and 2

Step 1 · The model both groups

Which model tests the training? The preregistered model:

anf_model <- lmer(AutonomyNonFrustrated ~ Occasion * condition +
                    (1 | Municipality/id),
                  data = df)

anf_fixed <- tidy(anf_model, effects = "fixed") |>
  select(term, b = estimate, se = std.error, df, p = p.value)

anf_fixed |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))
term b se df p
(Intercept) 6.000 0.236 28.779 0.000
OccasionT1 -0.015 0.189 731.690 0.937
OccasionT2 0.174 0.192 810.334 0.366
OccasionT3 0.297 0.200 793.261 0.138
conditionExperimental -0.065 0.337 29.923 0.848
OccasionT1:conditionExperimental -0.207 0.263 730.399 0.432
OccasionT2:conditionExperimental 0.040 0.289 789.433 0.889
OccasionT3:conditionExperimental 0.128 0.319 767.443 0.688

In January the control group averages 6.00 on the scale from 0 to 10; the experimental group starts 0.06 points lower, a difference that is not significant (p = .848).

Does the model pass the textbook checks? Convergence, the same fixed effects with two other optimizers, no variance at zero, residuals and person intercepts close to normal, and the spread of the residuals over condition and wave:

anf_checks <- lmm_checks(anf_model)
anf_checks
check value criterion holds
1 estimation: converged yes yes ✓
2 estimation: the same with bobyqa and Nelder-Mead converge, fixed effects within 0.0000004 within .001 ✓
3 variances: none at zero smallest SD 0.488 (Municipality) not singular ✓
4 residuals: skewness -.32 within ±2 ✓
5 residuals: excess kurtosis .39 below 7 ✓
6 person intercepts: skewness -.29 within ±2 ✓
7 residuals: largest / smallest SD of the eight cells 1.13 reported – 
plot_residuals(anf_model)

The model converges, two other optimizers give the same fixed effects, every variance lies above zero, and the residuals and the person intercepts stay within the bounds of normality; the residuals spread about evenly over condition and wave (the largest SD of a cell is 1.13 times the smallest).

Does the control group gain when it trains? The period-specific model, on the September and December waves:

condition test chisq df p

Next → Step 7, equivalence: Which random structure is the richest?

Step 7 · Equivalence both groups

Which random structure is the richest? The model of step 1 under the three structures, fitted with bobyqa, and the smallest variance of each:

rnf_structures <- list(
  `(1 | trainedBy/Municipality/id)` = rnf_trainer,
  `(1 | Municipality/id)` =
    lmer(RelatednessNonFrustrated ~ Occasion * condition +
           (1 | Municipality/id),
         data = df, control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")),
  `(1 | id)` =
    lmer(RelatednessNonFrustrated ~ Occasion * condition +
           (1 | id),
         data = df, control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")))

rnf_variances <- rnf_structures |>
  map(\(fit) as_tibble(VarCorr(fit))) |>
  list_rbind(names_to = "structure") |>
  summarise(smallest = min(vcov), .by = structure) |>
  mutate(above_zero = smallest >= 1e-8)

rnf_variances |>
  mutate(smallest = sprintf("%.1e", smallest))
structure smallest above_zero
(1 | trainedBy/Municipality/id) 0.0e+00 FALSE
(1 | Municipality/id) 2.0e-01 TRUE
(1 | id) 1.6e+00 TRUE 
# the first structure whose variances all lie above zero
rnf_richest <- rnf_variances$structure[rnf_variances$above_zero][1]

Do the groups really not differ? The two claims of absence, at baseline and after both trainings, with the preregistered and with the richest structure:

rnf_sd_T0 <- sd(df$RelatednessNonFrustrated[df$Occasion == "T0"], na.rm = TRUE)

rnf_tost <- bind_rows(
  preregistered = tidy(rnf_model, effects = "fixed"),
  richest       = tidy(rnf_structures[[rnf_richest]], effects = "fixed"),
  .id = "model") |>
  filter(term %in% c("conditionExperimental",
                     "OccasionT3:conditionExperimental")) |>
  transmute(model,
            claim   = if_else(term == "conditionExperimental", "baseline",
                              "after_both"),
            term,
            delta_d = estimate / rnf_sd_T0,
            se_d    = std.error / rnf_sd_T0,
            ci_low  = delta_d - qt(.95, df) * se_d,
            ci_high = delta_d + qt(.95, df) * se_d,
            p_tost  = pmax(pt((delta_d + sesoi) / se_d, df,
                              lower.tail = FALSE),
                           pt((delta_d - sesoi) / se_d, df)),
            p_two_sided = p.value,
            verdict = verdict_of(p_tost, p_two_sided))

rnf_tost |>
  select(model, claim, delta_d, ci_low, ci_high, p_tost, p_two_sided,
         verdict) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))
model claim delta_d ci_low ci_high p_tost p_two_sided verdict
preregistered baseline -0.061 -0.316 0.195 0.181 0.688 inconclusive
preregistered after_both 0.135 -0.081 0.350 0.308 0.303 inconclusive
richest baseline -0.061 -0.316 0.195 0.181 0.688 inconclusive
richest after_both 0.135 -0.081 0.350 0.308 0.303 inconclusive

Neither claim of absence can be shown. Both tests are inconclusive, as their intervals reach beyond ±0.20: at baseline Δd = -0.06, 90 % CI [-0.32, 0.19], after both trainings Δd = 0.13, 90 % CI [-0.08, 0.35]. The richest structure with all variances above zero is persons in municipalities, as in the preregistered model; it gives the same verdicts, and Δd stays the same to three decimals.

Next → Step 8, what follows: Where does the result go?

What follows · Step 8

Step 8 · What follows

Where does the result go? Relatedness Non-Frustrated shows no training effect in any model. Its interaction at T1 and its piecewise terms go to the comparison of the estimates in Chapter 20, its directional tests to the correction for many outcomes in 10.7.

5 Does the control group gain more while it trains? September to December: b = -0.12, p = .686; piecewise: b = 0.26, p = .276 random slopes
6 Does the change vary within a condition? 0 of 8 tests significant equivalence
7 Alike at baseline and after both trainings (TOST)? baseline: inconclusive; after both: inconclusive what follows

Next → Step 7, equivalence: Which random structure is the richest?

Step 7 · Equivalence both groups

Which random structure is the richest? The model of step 1 under the three structures, fitted with bobyqa, and the smallest variance of each:

emp_structures <- list(
  `(1 | trainedBy/Municipality/id)` = emp_trainer,
  `(1 | Municipality/id)` =
    lmer(Empowerment ~ Occasion * condition +
           (1 | Municipality/id),
         data = df, control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")),
  `(1 | id)` =
    lmer(Empowerment ~ Occasion * condition +
           (1 | id),
         data = df, control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")))

emp_variances <- emp_structures |>
  map(\(fit) as_tibble(VarCorr(fit))) |>
  list_rbind(names_to = "structure") |>
  summarise(smallest = min(vcov), .by = structure) |>
  mutate(above_zero = smallest >= 1e-8)

emp_variances |>
  mutate(smallest = sprintf("%.1e", smallest))
structure smallest above_zero
(1 | trainedBy/Municipality/id) 0.0e+00 FALSE
(1 | Municipality/id) 4.1e-02 TRUE
(1 | id) 6.2e-01 TRUE 
# the first structure whose variances all lie above zero
emp_richest <- emp_variances$structure[emp_variances$above_zero][1]

Do the groups really not differ? The two claims of absence, at baseline and after both trainings, with the preregistered and with the richest structure:

emp_sd_T0 <- sd(df$Empowerment[df$Occasion == "T0"], na.rm = TRUE)

emp_tost <- bind_rows(
  preregistered = tidy(emp_model, effects = "fixed"),
  richest       = tidy(emp_structures[[emp_richest]], effects = "fixed"),
  .id = "model") |>
  filter(term %in% c("conditionExperimental",
                     "OccasionT3:conditionExperimental")) |>
  transmute(model,
            claim   = if_else(term == "conditionExperimental", "baseline",
                              "after_both"),
            term,
            delta_d = estimate / emp_sd_T0,
            se_d    = std.error / emp_sd_T0,
            ci_low  = delta_d - qt(.95, df) * se_d,
            ci_high = delta_d + qt(.95, df) * se_d,
            p_tost  = pmax(pt((delta_d + sesoi) / se_d, df,
                              lower.tail = FALSE),
                           pt((delta_d - sesoi) / se_d, df)),
            p_two_sided = p.value,
            verdict = verdict_of(p_tost, p_two_sided))

emp_tost |>
  select(model, claim, delta_d, ci_low, ci_high, p_tost, p_two_sided,
         verdict) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))
model claim delta_d ci_low ci_high p_tost p_two_sided verdict

preregistered after_both 0.067 -0.118 0.252 0.118 0.551 inconclusive
richest baseline -0.204 -0.399 -0.009 0.513 0.087 inconclusive
richest after_both 0.067 -0.118 0.252 0.118 0.551 inconclusive

Neither claim of absence can be shown. Both tests are inconclusive, as their intervals reach beyond ±0.20: at baseline Δd = -0.20, 90 % CI [-0.40, -0.01], after both trainings Δd = 0.07, 90 % CI [-0.12, 0.25]. The richest structure with all variances above zero is persons in municipalities, as in the preregistered model; it gives the same verdicts, and Δd stays the same to three decimals.

  summarise(smallest = min(vcov), .by = structure) |>
  mutate(above_zero = smallest >= 1e-8)

ag_variances |>
  mutate(smallest = sprintf("%.1e", smallest))
structure smallest above_zero
(1 | trainedBy/Municipality/id) 3.2e-02 TRUE
(1 | Municipality/id) 8.5e-02 TRUE
(1 | id) 1.2e+00 TRUE 
# the first structure whose variances all lie above zero
ag_richest <- ag_variances$structure[ag_variances$above_zero][1]

Do the groups really not differ? The two claims of absence, at baseline and after both trainings, with the preregistered and with the richest structure:

ag_sd_T0 <- sd(df$Agency[df$Occasion == "T0"], na.rm = TRUE)

ag_tost <- bind_rows(
  preregistered = tidy(ag_model, effects = "fixed"),
  richest       = tidy(ag_structures[[ag_richest]], effects = "fixed"),
  .id = "model") |>
  filter(term %in% c("conditionExperimental",
                     "OccasionT3:conditionExperimental")) |>
  transmute(model,
            claim   = if_else(term == "conditionExperimental", "baseline",
                              "after_both"),
            term,
            delta_d = estimate / ag_sd_T0,
            se_d    = std.error / ag_sd_T0,
            ci_low  = delta_d - qt(.95, df) * se_d,
            ci_high = delta_d + qt(.95, df) * se_d,
            p_tost  = pmax(pt((delta_d + sesoi) / se_d, df,
                              lower.tail = FALSE),
                           pt((delta_d - sesoi) / se_d, df)),
            p_two_sided = p.value,
            verdict = verdict_of(p_tost, p_two_sided))

ag_tost |>
  select(model, claim, delta_d, ci_low, ci_high, p_tost, p_two_sided,
         verdict) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))
model claim delta_d ci_low ci_high p_tost p_two_sided verdict
preregistered baseline -0.121 -0.333 0.091 0.265 0.340 inconclusive
preregistered after_both 0.012 -0.201 0.225 0.074 0.925 inconclusive
richest baseline -0.120 -0.320 0.081 0.247 0.312 inconclusive
richest after_both 0.013 -0.200 0.226 0.074 0.920 inconclusive

Neither claim of absence can be shown. Both tests are inconclusive, as their intervals reach beyond ±0.20: at baseline Δd = -0.12, 90 % CI [-0.33, 0.09], after both trainings Δd = 0.01, 90 % CI [-0.20, 0.23]. The richest structure with all variances above zero keeps the trainer level, persons in municipalities in trainers; it gives the same verdicts, and Δd moves by at most 0.001.

The effects · Steps 3 to 5

Step 3 · The interactions both groups

Does the experimental group change more? The three interaction terms, with and without the trainer level:

ic_trainer_fixed <- tidy(ic_trainer, effects = "fixed") |>
  select(term, b_trainer = estimate, p_trainer = p.value)

  filter(str_detect(term, ":")) |>
  left_join(ic_trainer_fixed, by = "term")

ic_interactions |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))
term b se df p b_trainer p_trainer
OccasionT1:conditionExperimental 0.315 0.174 731.528 0.071 0.315 0.071
OccasionT2:conditionExperimental 0.231 0.192 787.481 0.229 0.231 0.229
OccasionT3:conditionExperimental 0.157 0.212 766.081 0.457 0.157 0.457

What does the model imply? The means of both groups at each wave; shaded the two training windows:

plot_means(ic_model)

By T1 the experimental group has not gained significantly more than the control group (b = 0.31, p = .071), nor by T2 (b = 0.23, p = .229). At T3, after the control group’s training, the groups do not differ significantly either (b = 0.16, p = .457). With the trainer level, the three terms stay the same to three decimals and keep their verdicts.

Next → Step 4, one-sided tests: Does it hold one-sided?

Step 4 · One-sided tests both groups

Does it hold one-sided? The effects at T1 and T2, where the hypotheses expect a positive sign:

ic_one_sided <- ic_interactions |>
  filter(term != "OccasionT3:conditionExperimental") |>
  transmute(term, b, p, p_one_sided = pt(b / se, df, lower.tail = FALSE))

ic_one_sided |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))
term b p p_one_sided
OccasionT1:conditionExperimental 0.315 0.071 0.035
OccasionT2:conditionExperimental 0.231 0.229 0.115

One-sided, the effect at T1 becomes significant (p = .035), the one at T2 non-significant (p = .115).

Next → Step 5, the replication: Does the control group gain when it trains?

Step 5 · The replication both groups

Does the control group gain when it trains? The period-specific model, on the September and December waves:

ic_period <- lmer(IntellectualCapital ~ condition * Time_T3 +
                    (1 | Municipality/id),
                  data = df_T23)

ic_period_terms <- tidy(ic_period, effects = "fixed") |>
  filter(str_detect(term, ":")) |>
  transmute(term, b = estimate, se = std.error, df, p = p.value,
            singular = isSingular(ic_period))

ic_period_terms |>
  mutate(p_one_sided = pt(-b / se, df, lower.tail = FALSE),
         across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))
term b se df p singular p_one_sided
conditionExperimental:Time_T3 -0.182 0.216 223.706 0.4 FALSE 0.2

And over all four waves? The piecewise model, with one time indicator for each training:

ic_piecewise <- lmer(IntellectualCapital ~ condition *
                       (Time_Exp_Training + Time_Control_Training) +
                       (1 | Municipality/id),
                     data = df)

ic_piecewise_terms <- tidy(ic_piecewise, effects = "fixed") |>
  filter(str_detect(term, ":")) |>
  transmute(term, b = estimate, se = std.error, df, p = p.value)

ic_piecewise_terms |>
  mutate(expected    = if_else(str_detect(term, "Time_Exp"), 1, -1),
         p_one_sided = pt(expected * b / se, df, lower.tail = FALSE),
         across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))
term b se df p expected p_one_sided
conditionExperimental:Time_Exp_Training 0.265 0.153 758.418 0.085 1 0.042
conditionExperimental:Time_Control_Training -0.094 0.194 739.938 0.627 -1 0.313

Between September and December, while the control group trains, it does not gain significantly more than the experimental group (b = -0.18, p = .400). In the piecewise model the experimental group’s training window shows no significant effect (b = 0.26, p = .085), and the control group’s window shows none either (b = -0.09, p = .627).

conditionExperimental:Time_Control_Training -0.511 0.139 748.530 0.00 -1 0.000

Between September and December, while the control group trains, it gains more than the experimental group (b = -0.56, p < .001). In the piecewise model the experimental group gains more while it trains (b = 0.24, p = .030), and the control group gains more while it trains (b = -0.51, p < .001).

What does a single indicator of being trained show? D is 1 once a person’s own group has trained (Chapter 2):

h1_D <- lmer(H1_ListeningTogetherness ~ D + (1 | Municipality/id),
             data = df)

tidy(h1_D, effects = "fixed") |>
  filter(term == "D") |>
  select(term, b = estimate, se = std.error, df, p = p.value) |>

term b se df p
D 0.548 0.054 791.977 0

Being trained goes with a score higher by 0.55 points (p < .001). Without time effects, D also takes up any general improvement over the year, so this is an upper bound of the training effect.

Step 6 · Random slopes both groups

Does the change vary within each condition? The eight tests of the script (10.2), four in each condition:

h1_slopes_within <- slopes_within |>

  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))

And across trainers and municipalities? Random slopes of both time contrasts at the trainer and municipality levels, against random intercepts, on maximum-likelihood fits:

h1_intercepts <- lmer(H1_ListeningTogetherness ~ TF_helmert + TS_helmert +
                        (1 | trainedBy/Municipality) + (1 | id),
                      data = df, REML = FALSE)
h1_slopes <- lmer(H1_ListeningTogetherness ~ TF_helmert + TS_helmert +
                    (TF_helmert + TS_helmert | trainedBy/Municipality) +

Next → Step 7, equivalence: Which random structure is the richest?

Step 7 · Equivalence both groups

Which random structure is the richest? The model of step 1 under the three structures, fitted with bobyqa, and the smallest variance of each:

h1_structures <- list(
  `(1 | trainedBy/Municipality/id)` = h1_trainer,
  `(1 | Municipality/id)` =
    lmer(H1_ListeningTogetherness ~ Occasion * condition +
           (1 | Municipality/id),
         data = df, control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")),
  `(1 | id)` =
    lmer(H1_ListeningTogetherness ~ Occasion * condition +
           (1 | id),
         data = df, control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")))

h1_variances <- h1_structures |>
  map(\(fit) as_tibble(VarCorr(fit))) |>
  list_rbind(names_to = "structure") |>
  summarise(smallest = min(vcov), .by = structure) |>
  mutate(above_zero = smallest >= 1e-8)

h1_variances |>
  mutate(smallest = sprintf("%.1e", smallest))
structure smallest above_zero
(1 | trainedBy/Municipality/id) 0.0e+00 FALSE
(1 | Municipality/id) 4.0e-02 TRUE
(1 | id) 5.9e-01 TRUE 
# the first structure whose variances all lie above zero
h1_richest <- h1_variances$structure[h1_variances$above_zero][1]

Do the groups really not differ? The two claims of absence, at baseline and after both trainings, with the preregistered and with the richest structure:

h1_sd_T0 <- sd(df$H1_ListeningTogetherness[df$Occasion == "T0"], na.rm = TRUE)

h1_tost <- bind_rows(
  preregistered = tidy(h1_model, effects = "fixed"),
  richest       = tidy(h1_structures[[h1_richest]], effects = "fixed"),
  .id = "model") |>
  filter(term %in% c("conditionExperimental",
                     "OccasionT3:conditionExperimental")) |>
  transmute(model,
            claim   = if_else(term == "conditionExperimental", "baseline",
                              "after_both"),
            term,
            delta_d = estimate / h1_sd_T0,
            se_d    = std.error / h1_sd_T0,
            ci_low  = delta_d - qt(.95, df) * se_d,
            ci_high = delta_d + qt(.95, df) * se_d,
            p_tost  = pmax(pt((delta_d + sesoi) / se_d, df,
                              lower.tail = FALSE),
                           pt((delta_d - sesoi) / se_d, df)),
            p_two_sided = p.value,
            verdict = verdict_of(p_tost, p_two_sided))

h1_tost |>
  select(model, claim, delta_d, ci_low, ci_high, p_tost, p_two_sided,
         verdict) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))
model claim delta_d ci_low ci_high p_tost p_two_sided verdict
preregistered baseline -0.020 -0.232 0.193 0.080 0.876 inconclusive
preregistered after_both -0.225 -0.434 -0.016 0.578 0.077 inconclusive
richest baseline -0.020 -0.232 0.193 0.080 0.876 inconclusive
richest after_both -0.225 -0.434 -0.016 0.578 0.077 inconclusive

Neither claim of absence can be shown. Both tests are inconclusive, as their intervals reach beyond ±0.20: at baseline Δd = -0.02, 90 % CI [-0.23, 0.19], after both trainings Δd = -0.23, 90 % CI [-0.43, -0.02]. The richest structure with all variances above zero is persons in municipalities, as in the preregistered model; it gives the same verdicts, and Δd stays the same to three decimals.

Next → Step 8, what follows: Where does the result go?

What follows · Step 8

Step 8 · What follows

Where does the result go? Listening and Togetherness reaches significance at T1 only one-sided, but shows the effect in both windows of the piecewise model and when the control group trains. Its interaction at T1 is the preregistered test of Hypothesis 1: 10.7 corrects it within the three composites, Chapter 14 repeats the model in every sample set, and Chapter 20 sets it beside the other estimates of the training effect.

Hypothesis 2: Cognitive Complexity

Its path through the steps. One row per step below, from the models of the steps, fitted once more; every step uses both groups both groups:

Step Question Result Next
1 Does the model pass the textbook checks? yes, all six random structure
2 Municipalities a level of their own? Trainers? municipalities: yes; trainers: no interactions
3 Does the experimental group change more (T1, T2, T3)? T1: b = 0.31, p = .000; T2: b = 0.05, p = .599; T3: b = -0.16, p = .140 one-sided tests
5 Does the control group gain more while it trains? September to December: b = -0.31, p = .003; piecewise: b = -0.33, p = .001 random slopes
6 Does the change vary within a condition? 2 of 8 tests significant equivalence
7 Alike at baseline and after both trainings (TOST)? baseline: inconclusive; after both: inconclusive what follows
8 Where next? Chapters 14 and 20; 10.7

The model · Steps 1 and 2

Step 1 · The model both groups

Which model tests the training? The preregistered model:

h2_fixed <- tidy(h2_model, effects = "fixed") |>
  select(term, b = estimate, se = std.error, df, p = p.value)

h2_fixed |>

In January the control group averages 8.22 on the scale from 0 to 10; the experimental group starts 0.10 points lower, a difference that is not significant (p = .386).

Does the model pass the textbook checks? Convergence, the same fixed effects with two other optimizers, no variance at zero, residuals and person intercepts close to normal, and the spread of the residuals over condition and wave:

h2_checks

The model converges, two other optimizers give the same fixed effects, every variance lies above zero, and the residuals and the person intercepts stay within the bounds of normality; the residuals spread about evenly over condition and wave (the largest SD of a cell is 1.27 times the smallest).

Step 3 · The interactions both groups

Does the experimental group change more? The three interaction terms, with and without the trainer level:

  select(term, b_trainer = estimate, p_trainer = p.value)

  filter(str_detect(term, ":")) |>

What does the model imply? The means of both groups at each wave; shaded the two training windows:

plot_means(h2_model)

By T1 the experimental group has gained more than the control group (b = 0.31, p < .001); by T2 the advantage has faded (b = 0.05, p = .599). At T3, after the control group’s training, the change since January no longer differs significantly (b = -0.16, p = .140). With the trainer level, the three terms move by at most 0.001 and keep their verdicts.
